AC Milan talent Akram Jadid is making a name for himself on the international stage, with a hat-trick for Morocco U17s.

At the Stadio Olimpico in Sousse, the Milan U18s striker scored a hat-trick in the 5-1 win over Tunisia. Not only that, but he got his three goals in just five minutes. It was a performance that promptly gained traction on social media, where videos of his goals are circulating widely.

Industry observers note that read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The match opened with Morocco taking the lead through Hatim Dabdoubi in the 24th minute. After half-time, Mohamed Aziz Abdelbaki levelled things on the hour mark, before Aymane Aït Hammou restored the lead with six minutes to go.

Industry observers note that then Jadid entered the scene. He netted 89th minute with his left foot, converted a penalty to make it 4-1 in the 92nd minute and completed his hat-trick in the 94th minute, scoring with his right foot.

He is one to look out for in the future, with promotion to the Primavera and eventually the Futuro seeming like a certainty at this point. He has trained with the first team, and went viral for having scored over 700 goals in the youth teams to this point.

Thomas Tuchel's 'best night' as England manager: Three Lions boss hails heroes after Spain victory - but hits out at Elliot Anderson decision made by referee he previously labelled a 'one out of 10'

📅 15 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (415 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 18:10 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 19:58 EST, 15 November 2026.
  • Thomas Tuchel hailed the 'best performance of my time as manager' after England beat world champions Spain in a crazy, brilliant see-sawing drama of a Nations League tie.
  • England played the best football of Tuchel's two-year reign as coach to end Spain's world record 43-match unbeaten run.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By OLIVER HOLT, CHIEF SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 18:10 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 19:58 EST, 15 November 2026.

Thomas Tuchel hailed the 'best performance of my time as manager' after England beat world champions Spain in a crazy, brilliant see-sawing drama of a Nations League tie.

England played the best football of Tuchel's two-year reign as coach to end Spain's world record 43-match unbeaten run.

England raced into a 3-0 lead with a penalty from Harry Kane, and further goals from Ezri Konsa and Ben White.

But they played the last half an hour of the game with ten men after Elliot Anderson was sent off for pulling back Lamine Yamal.

Spain got two goals back to set up a nerve-wracking finish but goalkeeper James Trafford, in the team ahead of Jordan Pickford, pulled off a miracle double save in the dying minutes to seal the win.

'What a performance we put out there for 60 minutes to be deservedly 3-0 up,' Tuchel remarked after the game. 'Thirty minutes against Spain with ten men feels like three hours.

Thomas Tuchel noted England's display in the win over Spain was the best in his time as boss.

According to recent reports, 'It was a statement victory. It was on the highest level football-wise. It is a wonderful feeling for us in the dressing room.

Recent findings suggest that 'It is the best performance of my time and they are unbeaten for 43 matches and that was a complete performance in that environment. To impose our identity on them was a real achievement.

It has been revealed that 'Declan Rice said he knew we were going to win and I could feel the true belief. This was the moment we wanted to prove ourselves. You need to rely on your teammates. That is why I am very proud of the win.'.

Tuchel also questioned the decision to give Anderson a straight red, made by a referee he once labelled a 'one out of 10'.

The Man City midfielder was sent off because Clement Turpin adjudged him not to have been making an attempt to play the ball when he fouled Yamal.

'The red card and the penalty is always a major decision and I needed to understand why it was a double punishment but... OK,' Tuchel told ITV Sport.

'From then it was a long 30 minutes but I don't want to focus on that because there were so, so many positives.'.

Tech Report: Significant revision emerges on Southampton’s latest contract talks with Tonda Eckert

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (525 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Southampton stuck by head coach Tonda Eckert after the Spygate saga.
  • It has been revealed that now, the club have confirmed that Eckert’s fresh deal at St Mary’s is done.
  • Eckert was appointed as the Saints’ permanent boss in December 2025 after an impressive spell as caretaker after Will Still’s sacking.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Southampton stuck by head coach Tonda Eckert after the Spygate saga. And, when his punishment of a suspended ban and fine was confirmed, it soon emerged that the Saints were preparing a new contract offer to secure the boss’ future beyond the end of the 2026/27 campaign.

It has been revealed that now, the club have confirmed that Eckert’s fresh deal at St Mary’s is done. His new contract will run until 2029, marking a two-year extension on his existing terms.

Eckert was appointed as the Saints’ permanent boss in December 2025 after an impressive spell as caretaker after Will Still’s sacking. The 33-year-old had only joined as U21s head coach in the summer, but his quick ascent has seen him emerge as one of Europe’s brightest coaching prospects.

Eckert’s breakthrough has been mightily impressive, despite the fact Spygate still casts a cloud over his Southampton record.

Sources indicate that after a string of roles in Germany and assistant manager positions at Barnsley and Genoa, Eckert’s step to become the Saints’ U21s boss was a good one for the trajectory of his career. Few saw him making such an early rise into the first-team role, but Still’s struggles and his success as caretaker meant he was swiftly solidified in his place as boss.

According to recent reports, he has averaged just under two points per game in his time as permanent head coach, and the four-point deduction his side started the season with is a thing of the past. That and a new contract for Eckert has helped lead the turmoil of Spygate in the past.

Importantly though, Eckert’s latest deal will fend off potential admirers. Clubs were bound to have him on the radar as he closed on the end of his contract, but a hefty compensation fee will now have to be paid to prise him away from the South Coast club.

Sources indicate that spygate will be brought up at every corner by opposing fans and it will have a place in English football history forever. Eckert will face questions about it for the foreseeable, and many will still debate that the punishment he faced was not strong enough.

Sources indicate that however, Eckert and the Saints are moving on by focusing on the long term and delivering success on the pitch. A new contract solidifies the club’s commitment to him despite the end to last season.

After losing 1-0 to Preston North End before the break, Eckert will be eager to see his side respond when they face Derby County this Saturday.

Coventry City vs. Crystal Palace - prediction, team news, lineups

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (745 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Seye Omidiora | 19 Nov 2026 14:06, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 14:12.
  • Thomas Frank's first assignment as Crystal Palace boss takes him to Coventry City for Saturday's gameweek 11 encounter at the Coventry Building Society Arena.
  • The Eagles manager's immediate priority will be lifting the South London side off the bottom of the Premier League table, a position that prompted Pierre Sage's swift departure after 10 top-flight matches.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Seye Omidiora | 19 Nov 2026 14:06, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 14:12.

Thomas Frank's first assignment as Crystal Palace boss takes him to Coventry City for Saturday's gameweek 11 encounter at the Coventry Building Society Arena.

The Eagles manager's immediate priority will be lifting the South London side off the bottom of the Premier League table, a position that prompted Pierre Sage's swift departure after 10 top-flight matches.

Palace have spent 14 consecutive seasons in the Premier League, and the capital club's board have taken drastic action to ensure that number becomes 15 at the end of the current campaign.

The Selhurst Park outfit entered the November international break in dire straits after a 3-1 loss to Andoni Iraola's Liverpool, marking their fourth consecutive top-flight defeat following setbacks against rivals Brighton & Hove Albion, Newcastle United and Tottenham Hotspur.

Particularly striking during that run were their struggles in front of goal and defensive frailties, highlighted by an alarming 12-1 aggregate score across those defeats that ultimately cost Sage his job.

Frank's reputation suffered during his spell as Spurs boss last season, but his previous work at Brentford should give the Selhurst Park faithful confidence that a turnaround is possible.

Nonetheless, it remains to be seen whether the Dane has conveyed his ideas in less than a week of training, with the international break also denying him access to his full squad, as the London club seek to end their four-match losing sequence.

A first victory since October and third overall would lift them above this weekend's 17th-placed hosts and potentially out of the bottom three, although the latter outcome depends on results elsewhere.

Coventry's 3-1 defeat at Everton before the pause left Frank Lampard's men alongside Arsenal and Manchester City as the only clubs yet to draw in this season's Premier League campaign.

However, while the defending champions and Man City occupy positions in the top three, Coventry's nine points leave them just one clear of the relegation places heading into a busy period.

Lampard's men can take encouragement from collecting six of those points in front of their adoring supporters, who witnessed October victories of 4-1 over Newcastle and 3-1 against Sunderland either side of a narrow 1-0 defeat to Fulham.

Although the absence of home clean sheets remains concerning, the Sky Blues' seven goals across their last three matches at the Coventry Building Society Arena represent clear progress after they failed to score in opening defeats to Hull City (1-0) and Brighton (5-0).

Now, the West Midlands side aim to secure consecutive home Premier League victories to avoid slipping into the bottom three.

Coventry City Premier League form:.

Crystal Palace Premier League form:.

Crystal Palace form (all competitions):.

Caleb Yirenkyi and Bobby Thomas (calf) are doubtful for Coventry this weekend, while Luke Woolfenden (knee) and Josh Eccles (ankle) face late fitness tests; however, Frank Onyeka, Aurele Amenda (calf), Haji Wright (thigh) and Ephron Mason-Clark (knee) are expected to miss out.

Jack Rudoni is the only home player to have scored more than once, with the attacking midfielder's three goals accounting for 30% of the Sky Blues' tally of 10 this term.

After registering assists in consecutive appearances against Newcastle and Spurs in October, Brandon Thomas-Asante has dropped to the bench, but the Ghanaian forward will hope to play a pivotal role for Lampard's team this weekend.

One Palace player denied the opportunity to make an immediate impression is Jean-Philippe Mateta, who serves the second game of a three-match suspension following his straight red card in October's 2-0 defeat at Spurs.

Further concerns surround Ismaila Sarr (groin) and Jorgen Strand Larsen (ankle), who are doubtful for this weekend's encounter and could leave Frank without several match-winners.

While former Arsenal defender Takehiro Tomiyasu (calf) is also touch-and-go for Saturday's match, Chadi Riad's knee injury will keep him sidelined until 2027.

Coventry City possible starting lineup:.

Rushworth; Van Ewijk, Mfuni, Pinnock, Dasilva; Torp, Grimes; Sakamoto, Rudoni, Gboho; Awoniyi.

Crystal Palace possible starting lineup:.

Henderson; Richards, Disasi, Lerma; Mingueza, Wharton, Timber, Mitchell; Kamada, Pino; Nketiah.

Frank's appointment should provide Palace with renewed purpose, but Mateta's suspension and doubts over Sarr and Strand Larsen leave the visitors short of attacking options.

Coventry have scored seven goals across their last three home matches and could exploit the Eagles' defensive uncertainty to spoil the Dane's first assignment.

Sometimes comments, however over the top, hit home. Michael Carrick will desperately hope the remark from his former Manchester United team-mate Gary Neville is not one of them. That it does not stick. That it does not come to define his time in charge of United this season – if he lasts this season. Or be used in one of those highlight reels, with doom-laden music, to explain the story of this Premier League campaign.

Industry observers note that on TV co-commentary duty for Sky, Neville referred to United as “blue mannequins” (they were wearing their away kit) and said that for a period after half-time it was the worst he had ever seen them play since he started watching, aged five. Neville is now 51. That is a lot of games to settle on this conclusion so strongly and, surely, inaccurately.

In a recent development, "They were absolutely mannequins!" Gary Neville says Michael Carrick has to stop defending the Manchester United players. pic.twitter.com/Pa4PqIoRbh.

According to recent reports, but so passive was their football that is the way he felt in the moment. For a club with United’s “attack, attack, attack” tradition – becoming something of a distant memory as seasons pass – that is a damning as it gets.

According to recent reports, neville’s Sky paymasters will be delighted by his emotive, insulting, headline-grabbing language. But he of course exaggerated a point to make a point. United, and Carrick, were, indeed, far too passive, lacking aggression, urgency and belief. They just do not press. United did, for too long, play like a team of dummies.

Against Fulham they almost played walking football until they conceded, desperation kicked in and they chased the game to salvage a late draw.

It begs the question: what is Carrick doing with this team? Yes, he may have been let down by no defensive signings in the summer – even if he must have bought into the proposal to prioritise a midfield rebuild – but he is far from absolved from blame.He will cling to the response to Lisandro Martínez’s own goal, to striking a post twice in the first half from Matheus Cunha and Bruno Fernandes, to managing to avoid a third successive defeat in a week, which would have led to the crisis klaxon being sounded. Carrick can talk about how ridiculous it would be to question his position as head coach. But is it?

We now go into a three-week international break and the Premier League vacuum would have been filled by a debate over Carrick’s future, whether he is up to the job and another existential examination as to where United are heading. And who is to blame.

Industry observers note that that still might happen. United did not lose. But they were not remotely good enough, as has been the case for most of the season. Their only league win in five was against newly promoted Ipswich Town, having lost to newly promoted Hull City. They have also drawn at Everton and now at Fulham, who started the day bottom of the table and remain winless. Apart from facing Manchester City, it has hardly been the most taxing of starts. Except they are down in 12th and have not played well at all.

It is not just that. Last year, United revamped their attack. Benjamin Sesko was absent through injury but are Cunha – despite his goal – Bryan Mbeumo and Marcus Rashford actually showing they are good enough? They, too, are passive and do not effect the play. Do not have that killer instinct. There is then an over-reliance on Fernandes. And if he does not do it, then who steps up?

That 15 minutes after half-time that culminated in the Martínez mishap was certainly woeful. But despite going close, United were also second best in the opening period, with Fulham’s 19-year-old academy product Josh King showing why he was so close to a senior England call-up. The forward ran riot, tormenting left-back Luke Shaw and was only denied by Senne Lammens. On more than one occasion, especially with a smart save with his right boot.

The goalkeeper was at the centre of Fulham’s goal, which was a shambles that summed up the state of United, who are just too easy to play against. And, so, Fulham’s captain Calvin Bassey was too strong for Cunha, who threw himself to the ground, looking for a foul, losing the ball from Kobbie Mainoo’s easy pass. The defender strode forward before Lammens parried his low shot, which then bounced off Martínez and back past the goalkeeper and into the net.

It was a Hammersmith End House of Horrors for United. To cap it all, Martínez then tried to blame Lammens who had, frankly, kept United in the game up until that point and could legitimately have told him where to go. And asked why he could not trap a ball and clear.

According to recent reports, "A horror at the Hammersmith end!"Lisandro Martínez puts the ball into his own net and Fulham lead! 😯 pic.twitter.com/jDmY4zL2XN.

In a recent development, fulham will certainly feel their own frustration. But with their newly introduced head coach Álvaro Arbeloa and an evolving team – if only striker Gonzalo García was more deadly – there are clear signs of optimism, having also just drawn at Liverpool.

United’s late equaliser was fortunate. Yes, they applied pressure but to no real effect until Cunha’s shot deflected off the boot of Fulham defender David Affengruber as he tried to block, to wrong-foot goalkeeper Bernd Leno, who had also been outstanding. It was credited to Cunha, his first of the season, and the relief from Carrick was understandably palpable.

Manchester United are LEVEL! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/DCxwlrzf1M.

But, once again, it was not up to the standard needed. And beyond the point, beyond the avoidance of defeat, that is the reality of where United are right now under Carrick who needs to step up, take more responsibility. And, like his team, be far less passive. Otherwise, he will not last.

Recent findings suggest that might these games offer less possession and more counter-attacking chances? That’s glass half full.

I was purely referring to the fact that they walked around the pitch. I’ve never seen a Manchester United team walk around on the pitch that much.

Sources indicate that michael has got to stop defending them. I get why he wants to defend them, he’s loyal, and there’s a long way to go into the season.

Both teams were the same, I called them mannequins. I’ve never seen United walk around so much out of possession, no alertness, no being on your toes.

I wish he could play those attacking players, but they are going to kill him defensively.

Neville goes on to call that period: “An absolute disgrace, nowhere near good enough.”.

Industry observers note that "They were absolutely mannequins!" Gary Neville states Michael Carrick has to stop defending the Manchester United players. pic.twitter.com/Pa4PqIoRbh.

I know Manchester United have a lot of individual quality, I have played against them for many years and know them really well. I know to be alert in case they shoot from distance. When you make some saves in the game you feel very focused. Unfortunately I couldn’t keep out the goal but that is football.

I didn’t think we were. Did you think we were? Football is a difficult game. We controlled a lot of the first half. It’s the Premier League and you will have spells where you don’t have it all your own way. To expect total dominance for the whole game, I don’t think anyone gets that in this league.

Industry observers note that I thought we should have won the game, I thought we created enough to win the game. The goal we did concede is one of them goals. The boys could have thought it is one of those days but I really like the reaction. We nearly won it in the end. We came to get the win of course, the way it panned out and the way we finished is the positive we take from it.

I think we did a good game. Obviously not an easy game for us, we were in the bottom position but we saw personality with the ball, we were brave. We had moments where we had to defend but in general we did a good game.

We wanted to control the transition and the counter attacks. We know they put too many people inside so we have to control the space behind our midfielders. They sometimes found the spaces, it is a difficult match against a substantial team and for me they will be near the top of the league by the end of the season.

According to recent reports, now we have to find the first victory. If you see our first five games we have already played Man Utd, Chelsea, at Anfield, at Sunderland. Now we have an October that will be so key for us.

It has been revealed that there were so many things for them, you can see it in the foul by [Harry] Maguire. Every decision was for them. I knew after the game against Manchester City that they don’t like Manchester United to lose.

It’s hard to explain, I feel after the first half we always get a lot of chances and create, play well.

It has been revealed that in the beginning of the second half they put in more energy than us and we cannot accept this. We always play better after conceding goal, and it cannot be like this.

Recent findings suggest that I don’t think today was about final decisions, we were a bit unlucky, I hit the post, and Bruno hit the post. We need to create more and hope the luck comes and we score. We need to improve in every single position.

Industry observers note that it was too slow, Fulham ran more and looked like they wanted to win more. Bassey just eased Cunha out the way [for Fulham’s goal] and looked like he wanted to take the game to Man United and Carrick will be thinking ‘we need to do a lot more’.

It was a game that was a real struggle for both teams. Both lacked confidence. There were challenges for both managers coming into this game, they both need the international break to start their seasons again.

It has been revealed that the defensive work from both teams was awful and lacked effort. Carrick will be relieved going back to Manchester with a goal and a point.

Michael Carrick has more work to do during the interval than Fulham’s Alvaro Arbeloa and cannot be happy with how defensively vulnerable his team and but also how wasteful they are in front of goal.

The truth is Matheus Cunha, Bryan Mbeumo and Marcus Rashford simply have to do more and dominate games. We are yet to see that form them this season and, apart from Lisandro Martinez forcing a fine save from Bernd Leno, Fulham have carried the greater threat here.

United get the game under way at Craven Cottage.

Very difficult to predict what you are going to be served by either of these teams. Both of their seasons are on a knife edge even at the this early juncture.

Sources indicate that if Manchester United could choose a Premier League away fixture to revitalise their season, Fulham would be it. Not just because they are bottom of the league with just one point, albeit impressively earned last week away to Liverpool, but because United have not been beaten at Craven Cottage since December 2009 – although, not such a good omen for United, is the fact that Michael Carrick was in their team that day (playing at centre-back).

Michael Carrick dismissed as “ridiculous” any suggestion that his job as Manchester United’s head coach was at risk this early in the season. But he needs a positive result today against Fulham otherwise much of the prolonged international break will be taken up by debate as to whether he is up to it. United do not play again after today until they host stricken Tottenham Hotspur on October 10 and their start to this season has simply not been good enough. The concern for Carrick appears his inability to positively affect games when things are going against United.

In a recent development, the script pretty much writes itself these days. A flicker of optimism and hope of a fresh start giving way to the same old frustrations, complaints and inquests, the cumulative toll of which places an ever greater strain on a club mired in mediocrity but with little reprieve from the expectations that come with bearing such an illustrious name.

Michael Carrick states Pro Ref’s apology over the derby fiasco means little to Manchester United – but warned his players they cannot allow such setbacks to derail their season.

Chief refereeing officer Howard Webb formally apologised to United after the VAR officials Matt Donohue and Blake Antrobus failed to spot Enzo Fernandez was offside before wrongly allowing Erling Haaland’s winning goal to stand in Manchester City’s 1-0 victory at Old Trafford.

United were left shocked by the scale of the blunder, which came with 30 minutes of the game remaining and City already down to 10 men.

But Carrick has told his players not to become preoccupied with such injustices as they bid to overcome their poor start to the season before a crucial trip to Craven Cottage.

“It can have an impact in the moment of time, it can have a significant impact, but we can’t let it have an impact on the rest of the season,” the United manager remarked.

In a recent development, “That’s for us to get back to winning ways as soon as possible. Listen, one-off things can happen, at the time it was a pretty massive one, we know that. I don’t think I need to go over that.

“But yeah, I’ve got faith in it [VAR], it’s the system that we work towards and that we use so the apology doesn’t mean an awful lot.”.

Carrick added: “I can appreciate and I respect it for them putting their hands up and saying we got that wrong, I think it happens - it does happen.

“But moving forward, yeah, we just have to deal with it, what’s thrown in front of us. And maybe we get one or two decisions on the back of how it balances out - percentages or law of averages or whatever that may be.

“But that was a pretty major one to take and had a huge impact on that game and that’s why it was particularly tough.”.

Michael Carrick may have had a point when he said it was “ridiculous” to question his future this early in the season, but this afternoon’s game at Fulham will shape the mood at Manchester United for the next three weeks.

A tally of four points from their first four games of the season is a disappointing start, and Brighton added to the sense of gloom in the League Cup by becoming the first side in 50 years to win from 2-0 down at Old Trafford.

With Champions League football on the agenda, that competition was at the bottom of United’s priority list but the ragged nature of the performance prompted boos around the stadium.

The no-show at Hull and defeat to 10-man City also fall into the “it’s how you lose” category of defeat, while there are widening fissures between the fanbase and the club’s hierarchy over ticketing policy and Sir Jim Ratcliffe’s political interventions.

The mood has also been sour at Fulham in the first few weeks of the season. In fact, they start the game bottom of the Premier League with one point, but do have the incentive of knowing a draw would take them above Spurs.

Following reports of friction between some established players and upcoming head coach Alvaro Arbeloa though, they produced their best performance of the season in a goalless draw at Anfield last week when they had chances to win the game.

Fulham made nine changes in the League Cup in mid-week, but still ran out 3-2 winners at West Ham. Despite the west London club being an established mid-table Premier League team for a number of seasons, and United’s vulnerable state for the past few years, Fulham have beaten their opponent’s just once in the league since December 2009.Full team news on the way shortly.

Reading vs Bromley - prediction, team news, lineups

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (523 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Matthew Cooper | 19 Nov 2026 14:34.
  • Reading will be looking to get back to winning ways when they welcome Bromley to the Select Car Leasing Stadium on Saturday.
  • The hosts currently sit seventh in the League One table, while the visitors are rock bottom in 24th.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Matthew Cooper | 19 Nov 2026 14:34.

Reading will be looking to get back to winning ways when they welcome Bromley to the Select Car Leasing Stadium on Saturday.

The hosts currently sit seventh in the League One table, while the visitors are rock bottom in 24th.

Reading will be looking for an immediate response after suffering a 3-1 defeat to fellow promotion contenders Stockport County last weekend.

Jack Marriott equalised for the Royals after Kyle Wootton had opened the scoring, but goals from Ethan Ennis and Jack Diamond ultimately earned an notable victory for the Hatters.

That result saw Leam Richardson's side drop out of the playoff places, although they could return to the top six with a victory over Bromley if other results go their way.

Reading have now lost their last two league games, having also been beaten 2-0 by local rivals Oxford United, but they remain one of the most dangerous sides in the division.

The Royals have scored 26 goals in 15 league games so far, a number only eclipsed by four other teams, and the return of top scorer Marriott from injury has come as a welcome boost.

The veteran striker has scored in his last two games across all competitions and bagged a total of nine goals in 10 league games.

Bromley, meanwhile, have struggled to make the step up to League One and are bottom of the division with just nine points from 13 games.

The Ravens are without a win in their last 10 games across all competitions and upcoming manager Karl Robinson claims they "need to evolve" and "stick together" if they are to stay up this season.

Bromley's trip to Reading will be Robinson's first league game in charge, following a 2-0 defeat to Rotherham United in the FA Cup and a 2-1 defeat to MK Dons in the EFL Trophy.

It is worth noting that Bromley have never beaten Reading in a competitive fixture, although they did draw 1-1 in the EFL Cup earlier this season before the Royals triumphed on penalties.

Reading form (all competitions):.

Bromley form (all competitions):.

Reading will be able to welcome back Paudie O'Connor and Andy Rinomhota from suspension and they should come straight into the side.

Marriott is expected to lead the line, with support out wide from Kyreece Lisbie and Daniel Kyerewaa.

Victor Adeboyejo remains a doubt for Bromley after he suffered an injury in the warm-up ahead of the Rotherham game, meaning Michael Cheek is likely to start up front against Reading.

Jodi Jones and Mickel Miller are set to continue out wide, with George Saville and Kamil Conteh starting in midfield.

Reading possible starting lineup:.

Pereira; Godwin-Malife, O'Connor, Knight, Roberts; Wing, Rinomhota; Lisbie, Savage, Kyerewaa; Marriott.

Bromley possible starting lineup:.

George; Ifill, Grant, Taylor, Mendy; Saville, Conteh; Jones, McKiernan, Miller, Cheek.

Reading boast a strong attacking record this season and should have enough to beat a struggling Bromley side, despite the fact they have lost their last two league games.

#3022. Grief-stricken Tenerife stars return to action for first time since death of Jesus de Miguel, 30, after fatal on-field collision with goalkeeper: Tributes paid and match paused in 9th minute on emotional day

📅 15 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (625 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dailymail ↗ Open Full Page

Grief-stricken Tenerife stars return to action for first time since death of Jesus de Miguel, 30, after fatal on-field collision with goalkeeper: Tributes paid and match paused in 9th minute on emotional day

📅 15 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (625 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 14:11 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 21:21 EST, 15 November 2026.
  • Tenerife have returned to action for the first time since Spanish footballer Jesus de Miguel was tragically killed in a collision during a game with FC Andorra earlier this month.
  • Goalkeeper Jesus Owono came flying out of his goal and wiped out De Miguel with a high challenge, which resulted in the striker being admitted to intensive care, where he later died.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By LEWIS BROWNING, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 14:11 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 21:21 EST, 15 November 2026.

Tenerife have returned to action for the first time since Spanish footballer Jesus de Miguel was tragically killed in a collision during a game with FC Andorra earlier this month.

Goalkeeper Jesus Owono came flying out of his goal and wiped out De Miguel with a high challenge, which resulted in the striker being admitted to intensive care, where he later died.

Thirteen days on from the incident, Tenerife played their first game since the player's death as they took on AD Ceuta CF in LaLiga Hypermotion action – with the game filled with tributes to the star.

Players gave a floral tribute as they arrived for the match, and gathered outside gate nine of the Heliodoro Rodríguez Lopez Stadium – the shirt number he wore.

Grief-stricken Tenerife stars, meanwhile, took to the field carrying a bouquet of flowers, and placed it at the scene of the incident.

Both sets of players and fans then observed a minute's silence in memory of De Miguel before the game kicked off.

🕊️❤️ THE NINTH MINUTE BELONGED TO JESÚS DE MIGUEL! 🥹🏟️ Football took a back seat during Tenerife's first match following his passing.👏 In the ninth minute, the stadium came together in a heartfelt tribute to honor his memory.💔 Some losses are felt far beyond the pitch.… pic.twitter.com/mqPy4aE9Q3.

CF Tenerife returned to action for the first time since the death of Jesus de Miguel in a game flooded with tributes.

Both sets of players gathered around the centre circle before the game to pay tribute.

The forward (pictured in 2025) passed away after being on the receiving end of a brutal tackle.

The game was then brought to a pause in the ninth minute, so the players could pay another tribute.

Fans inside the stadium unveiled a tifo which read: 'Jesus de Miguel, 9, eternal blanquiazul', which translates to: 'Jesus de Miguel, 9, eternally white and blue.'.

Industry observers note that other fans held up white and blue cards beside the tifo, with others in the ground applauding. When Tenerife scored, De Miguel's shirt was held in the air.

After the game, which Tenerife won 2-0, both teams gathered in the centre circle to place De Miguel's shirt on a bouquet of flowers, and the fans applauded to bring an end to an emotional day.

The tragedy occurred as the game against Andorra entered the seventh minute of stoppage time, when De Miguel looked set to race away on the counter-attack for Tenerife in search of a winner.

As he watched a long ball drop into his path, the striker was struck in the chest by Owono's flying knee as he attempted to clear the ball near the halfway line.

After initially rolling around on the floor, De Miguel became motionless, and medical staff rushed onto the pitch to attend to him.

Owono was initially given a red card for the challenge before the decision was soon taken by the referee to abandon the fixture. Fans have chanted 'murderer' in his direction.

Before the game, players gathered outside gate nine - the shirt numebr de Miguel wore.

Goalkeeper Jesus Owono has been handed a 12-match ban and may never play football again.

On Friday, the goalkeeper was hit with a 12-match ban - but may never play again.

His manager Carles Manso has stated: 'We will ​give him space so that he feels completely free to make ‌any ⁠decision, whether he wants to return, when, or if he does not want to return.

'When he feels it is appropriate and when ​he feels genuinely ready to take a ​decision ⁠like that (he will do so).'.

By Matthew Cooper | 19 Nov 2026 14:42.

Cambridge United will be looking to pick up an notable victory when they welcome Stockport County to the Cledara Abbey Stadium on Saturday.

The hosts right now sit 10th in the League One table, while the visitors are second.

Cambridge United head into Saturday's clash looking to end a run of four league games without a victory.

The U's were thumped 3-0 by Leyton Orient in their most recent league game, but bounced back with an emphatic 6-0 victory over Brighton and Hove Albion Under-21s in the EFL Trophy.

However, that was followed by a 2-0 defeat to Bristol Rovers in the first round of the FA Cup and Neil Harris's side will be keen to produce a much-improved performance against Stockport.

It is worth noting that Cambridge have only lost once to Stockport in their last seven meetings across all competitions dating back to 2011.

Stockport, meanwhile, arrive at the Cledara Abbey Stadium in excellent form after suffering just one defeat in their last 12 games across all competitions.

In their most recent game, Stockport beat fellow promotion contenders Reading 3-1 thanks to goals from Kyle Wootton, Ethan Ennis and Jack Diamond.

That victory saw Jimmy McNulty's side go level on points with league leaders Huddersfield Town, although the Terriers have a superior goal difference and a game in hand.

Stockport have scored more goals than any other League One side so far this season with 29 and Wootton is the division's second-highest scorer with 10.

Louis Appere is expected to lead the line for Cambridge and will be looking to bag his first league goal since the first game of the season.

Ben Knight and Sullay Kaiki are likely to start out wide, with Raees Bangura-Williams set to continue in the No.10 role.

Stockport are expected to continue with the same side that beat Reading, with Wootton starting up front.

Diamond and Harry Wood are likely to start out wide, with Oliver Norwood and Lewis Bate set to start in midfield.

Cambridge United possible starting lineup:.

Eastwood; Bennett, Bauer, Watts, Bradshaw; Moxon, Ruddock-Mpanzu; Knight, Bangura-Williams, Kaiki; Appere.

Stockport County possible starting lineup:.

Whatmuff; Gordon, O'Connell, Pye; Ennis, Bate, Norwood, Osborn; Diamond, Wootton, Wood.

Stockport are in excellent form and should have enough to beat a Cambridge side that are without a win in their last four league games.

Bolton Wanderers team news and predicted XI vs Portsmouth with defensive reshuffle needed to improve leaky backline

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (560 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Bolton Wanderers return from the international break looking to pick themselves up from a demoralising defeat to Derby County two weeks ago.
  • Recent findings suggest that the biggest problem for the Trotters is their home form.
  • Sources indicate that whilst Bolton Wanderers have been trending down, it is the opposite for Portsmouth.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bolton Wanderers return from the international break looking to pick themselves up from a demoralising defeat to Derby County two weeks ago. Steven Schumacher’s team sit seven points above the bottom three but risk sliding at pace if they can’t begin to fix their defensive woes, having conceded 29 goals so far.

Recent findings suggest that the biggest problem for the Trotters is their home form. BWFC have lost all but two of seven games at the Toughsheet Community Stadium, conceding 15 of their 29 goals at the ground. Wanderers have to find form at home, and will hope Saturday’s game can be the start.

Sources indicate that whilst Bolton Wanderers have been trending down, it is the opposite for Portsmouth. Despite losing 2-1 to Stoke City before the break, Pompey have won three of their last six, sitting just two points off the top eight.

John Mousinho’s side head to Bolton with a good record against their opponents and will be hopeful of returning to winning ways at 15:00 on Saturday.

Bolton Wanderers have welcomed back all four internationals without any injury concern.

According to recent reports, thierry Gale and Chris Forino, who faced each other whilst playing for Barbados and Saint Lucia, both came back unscathed. The same can be noted for Gaizka Larrazabal and Josh Sheehan, who both played one game for their respective nations.

Eoin Toal and Gavin Bazunu could be available on Saturday after training this week.

Bazunu in particular could be a massive boost for BWFC. Whilst Jack Bonham has proven to be a solid deputy, the Irishman has been an astute signing from Southampton, preventing 1.45 expected goals and claiming two clean sheets this season.

Elsewhere John McAtee, Ryan Hardie, Jayden Nelson and Ethan Erhahon all remain out injured.

Bonham; Stephenson, Forino, Davies, Famewo; Sheehan, Simons; Larrazabal, Rodrigues, Gale; Dalby.

In a recent development, with Bazunu’s full status as of yet unconfirmed, Bonham keeps his place, but the defence is reshuffled. Akin Famewo moves to left-back in place of Max Conway, with Ben Davies taking his position in central defence.

According to recent reports, bolton Wanderers have need to stop conceding easy goals and they have performed better playing one central defender on either side of the back four. Famewo has done so before and played well. On Saturday, he will have the task of handling Adrian Segecic and Terry Devlin on the Pompey right.

Gaizka Larrazabal continues at right-wing having been one of Wanderers’ better players at Pride Park, whilst Gale also keeps his place, simply because he is one of the only wide men who often tracks back, something BWFC need to stop their defensive issues.

Bolton Wanderers’ clash with Portsmouth kicks off at 15:00 on Saturday afternoon.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Fabio Capello recalled what Franco Baresi meant to him as a player and captain, while commenting on Gerry Cardinale’s bold declarations too.

Few players mean more to a club – if any – than Baresi meant to Milan. The centre-back reinvented the role and became a symbol of one of the most dominant eras in the history of the sport, as well as an icon in the eyes of the fans who adored him.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Capello was lucky enough to coach the No.6 and he spoke about Baresi’s greatness on Andrea Longoni’s YouTube channel ‘Milan Hello’. His words were relayed by MilanNews, and the emotion was clear in his voice.

In a recent development, “He was key for what he conveyed to the other players when they came to play for Milan. I’m talking about champions, important players, foreigners, of all qualities. They saw in him the man who conveyed the history of Milan,” he remarked.

“Franco didn’t talk much in the dressing room, but when he did, he was listened to because you could feel his words came from the heart, you could feel they were something vital for everyone.”.

Last night, Capello was interviewed by Sky and he commented on Cardinale’s words, who has been making some quite bold pledges about Milan’s future in recent weeks.

It has been revealed that “He’s promising a lot with his words, I read everything he claims. Now I’m waiting for him, I’m waiting for the results. I want to see if he’ll do what he’s saying, if he has a proposal and a real idea of ​​where he wants to get to.

According to recent reports, “Berlusconi had also promised great things, but then he surrounded himself with people who knew about football. Besides the players, you also need to create a staff that follows you and understands your ideas.

“Now I don’t know if this staff has already been chosen, he keeps talking about latest sporting directors, about new people who will join Milan. Let’s see what he can do. The promises are great, we’ll see what the results will be.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Carter White | 19 Nov 2026 14:43.
  • Barcelona have reportedly earmarked Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez and two other defenders as transfer targets ahead of the January window.
  • Hansi Flick's men have enjoyed an excellent start to the 2026-27 campaign on the domestic scene, winning 11 of their opening 12 top-flight contests, meaning that they sit top of the La Liga standings.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Carter White | 19 Nov 2026 14:43.

Barcelona have reportedly earmarked Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez and two other defenders as transfer targets ahead of the January window.

Hansi Flick's men have enjoyed an excellent start to the 2026-27 campaign on the domestic scene, winning 11 of their opening 12 top-flight contests, meaning that they sit top of the La Liga standings.

Barca have been linked heavily to newly introduced defensive additions in recent times, including Tottenham Hotspur man Pedro Perro, however, it is believed that the Catalans are not pursuing a deal for the World Cup winner in the New Year.

Head coach Flick is supposedly targeting the signing of a centre-back and a full-back during the upcoming trading point, aiming to strengthen his side's chances of winning the Champions League for the first time since 2015.

Hoping to record four consecutive competitive victories, Barcelona welcome Europe-chasing Villarreal to Camp Nou on Sunday afternoon, when club action will return following the international break.

As per Spanish publication Mundo Deportivo, Barcelona will press forward in their search for a newly introduced defender during the January transfer window, in which head coach Flick is expected to be backed by sporting director Deco.

The report claims that Barca are keen on the cost-effective option of bringing Manchester United centre-back Martinez to the club, with the 2022 World Cup winner approaching the end of his contract at Old Trafford.

As well as the outspoken United star, it is understood that the La Liga leaders are also eyeing up a move for Borussia Dortmund's Nico Schlotterbeck, who is capable of playing at centre-back and left-back.

The 26-year-old was given his senior Germany debut by Barca boss Flick in March 2022, and the Dortmund sweetheart is supposedly available for £50m ahead of the winter transfer window.

Finally, it is believed that Barca's hierarchy are yet to shelve the possibility of signing Inter Milan and Italy defender Alessandro Bastoni, who is noted to be open to a La Liga switch amid a £33m valuation.

After his explosive comments following defeat by Atletico Madrid in the Champions League, Martinez created a major rift between himself and the Manchester United board, as well as former head coach Carrick.

The general consensus is that the 28-year-old's time at Old Trafford is up, and it would be surprising if the Red Devils triggered the extension clause in the defender's current contract.

That being stated, the arrival of compatriot Mauricio Pochettino could hand Martinez a second chance this season, with the centre-back potentially playing himself back into favour at the Theatre of Dreams.

Mauricio Pochettino swaps one football for another as fresh Man United boss continues US farewell tour at NFL clash ahead of final game in charge

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (567 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 22:54 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 22:55 EST, 15 November 2026.
  • Mauricio Pochettino's United States farewell tour continued on Sunday night with a pitstop at an NFL showdown.
  • The manager has one game left in charge of the United States before parting ways with the national team to join Manchester United after agreeing a deal with the Premier League club earlier this week.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By ISABEL BALDWIN, US ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR.

Published: 22:54 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 22:55 EST, 15 November 2026.

Mauricio Pochettino's United States farewell tour continued on Sunday night with a pitstop at an NFL showdown.

The manager has one game left in charge of the United States before parting ways with the national team to join Manchester United after agreeing a deal with the Premier League club earlier this week.

The Argentine will replace Michael Carrick at Old Trafford on a two-and-a-half year contract after United agreed to pay more than £10million ($13m) to buy him and his backroom staff out of their contracts with the US Soccer Federation.

Recent findings suggest that before his return to England, the 54-year-old is enjoying his swansong with the US. In between overseeing his final games in charge of the national team, Pochettino was spotted soaking in the action of the other variety of football.

The former Tottenham Hotspur boss attended the primetime NFL showdown between the Cincinnati Bengals and Pittsburgh Steelers at Paycor Stadium in Cincinnati, Ohio on Sunday night.

The head coach, sporting his blue USSF coat, was captured standing on the sidelines with members of his staff ahead of the Sunday Night Football matchup.

USMNT and future Manchester United head coach Mauricio Pochettino is at the Bengals-Steelers game 😭🇺🇸 pic.twitter.com/B7Irn0YLnd.

Mauricio Pochettino's United States farewell tour continued at the NFL on Sunday night.

The new Manchester United boss attended the Cincinnati Bengals' game at Paycor Stadium.

He was greeted by kicker Evan McPherson, long snapper William Wagner and punter Ryan Rehkow - members of the Bengals' special teams - on the turf before kickoff.

The US is set to face Haiti in the second-leg of their CONCACAF Nations League quarterfinal at TQL Stadium in Cincinnati on Tuesday.

The game, which will take place around a mile north of the Bengals' Paycor Stadium, will mark Pochettino's final match in charge of the US national team.

He also took charge of the USA's 6-0 first-leg win against Haiti on Tuesday, which marked the first stop on his farewell tour.

Pochettino will begin his new role with Manchester United on Wednesday, immediately following Tuesday's second-leg. His first game will be against Liverpool at Anfield next Sunday.

He emotionally addressed his departure from the US setup and impending upcoming job in a press conference on Friday.

Flanked by US Soccer Federation bosses at the team’s headquarters in Georgia, an emotional Pochettino wiped away tears as he thanked the players and staff.

‘I haven't prepared a speech, I'm talking with my heart,’ he said. ‘It's difficult for me to talk now because I am a very emotional guy.

The Argentine was captured on the sidelines ahead of the game against the Pittsburgh Steelers.

Recent findings suggest that ‘When these moments arrive, it is always tough. Normally it is the opposite – you have been sacked! You cry because you want to stay.

‘I think it was one of the most difficult decisions of our career, but you have to move forward.

‘Not too many opportunities can happen in your career with a side like Manchester United. That is difficult to turn down when it arrives.

‘In some part it’s a very sad decision, in another part we are professional and we are trying to make our dreams come true. We are excited for that step forward.'.

Tech Report: Celtic vs St Mirren - prediction, team news, lineups

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (889 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Calum Burrowes | 19 Nov 2026 14:47, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 20:19.
  • Returning to action following the final international break of the year, St Mirren make the short journey to Celtic on Saturday looking for a victory that could draw them level on points with the teams in the top half of the Scottish Premiership.
  • The Bhoys entered the break with a return to winning ways in the league courtesy of a narrow 1-0 victory over bottom-placed Kilmarnock, while the Buddies suffered their second consecutive defeat with a home loss to Rangers.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Calum Burrowes | 19 Nov 2026 14:47, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 20:19.

Returning to action following the final international break of the year, St Mirren make the short journey to Celtic on Saturday looking for a victory that could draw them level on points with the teams in the top half of the Scottish Premiership.

The Bhoys entered the break with a return to winning ways in the league courtesy of a narrow 1-0 victory over bottom-placed Kilmarnock, while the Buddies suffered their second consecutive defeat with a home loss to Rangers.

After securing a record-extending 56th Scottish top-flight title on a dramatic final day of the season in May, Celtic began the 2026-27 campaign hoping for more of the same, retaining Martin O'Neill as manager, and he will take charge of his 339th game at the helm this weekend.

While they right now sit top of the Scottish Premiership with a four-point cushion over arch-rivals Rangers, their season has been far from straightforward, with the Bhoys entering the international break having recorded just one league victory in their previous three outings.

A home draw against Dundee United was followed by a defeat away to Falkirk, their first loss to the Bairns in nearly two decades, before they were presented with an opportunity to return to winning ways against basement side Kilmarnock, although their eventual 1-0 victory was far from convincing.

O'Neill's side took the lead through Republic of Ireland international Liam Scales but were made to work hard for all three points against a team that has won just twice all season.

Celtic have struggled even more in Europe, with just one victory from their opening four Europa League matches leaving them 32nd in the 36-team league phase and facing an uphill battle to reach the knockout stages.

Meanwhile, St Mirren have endured a difficult spell since their 2-1 defeat to Celtic in September, losing seven of their subsequent nine league matches and collecting fewer points than any other side in the division during that period, although their early-season results have at least kept them clear of the bottom two.

Led by Craig McLeish, who took charge on a permanent basis in June, the Buddies have won four, drawn two and lost seven of their opening 13 league fixtures, with the teams below them potentially able to close the gap through games in hand.

While they secured a narrow victory over Dundee in October, St Mirren have collected just one point from their subsequent three top-flight outings, extending their disappointing run of form.

The appointment of a young manager with ambitions of introducing a progressive style of football has yet to produce the desired results, with the Buddies' 12 goals scored representing the joint-lowest total in the division, while their 22 conceded is the second-highest.

After beating Kilmarnock 1-0 in early September, St Mirren sat second in the table with 10 points from a possible 12, but collecting just four more across their next nine matches has brought their promising start to a halt, although that early form provides a platform for McLeish's side to build on if they can rediscover their confidence.

Celtic Scottish Premiership form:.

Celtic form (all competitions):.

St Mirren Scottish Premiership form:.

Unlike their upcoming opponents, Celtic had several players away on international duty over the past fortnight and may need to make changes depending on their fitness following the additional travel.

Auston Trusty recently took a break from football following the death of his father and has not featured for O'Neill's side since their 4-1 Europa League defeat to Benfica in October.

However, he scored for the USA against Haiti during the international break and dedicated his goal to his father, potentially putting himself in contention for a return this weekend.

Alistair Johnston would have travelled to North America to join up with the Canada squad but remains sidelined with a hamstring injury sustained during a 2-1 victory over Hibernian at the end of October.

The Canadian full-back and German midfielder Mika Baur are O'Neill's only expected absentees, although it remains to be seen whether Kasper Hogh will retain his place up front after failing to score for the 16th consecutive match last time out.

As for St Mirren, they could name the same starting XI for a second consecutive match, although McLeish may be tempted to make changes following the two-week break.

Nikolas Agrafiotis, Malik Dijksteel and Keanu Baccus have all been sidelined through injury but are expected to return in the coming weeks, with Saturday potentially coming too soon for some of the trio.

Jonah Ayunga is also unavailable through injury and is not expected to return until early 2027.

Celtic possible starting lineup:.

Johnstone; Donovan, Carter-Vickers, Scales, Tierney; McGregor, Baur; Duran, Nygren, Jota; Hogh.

St Mirren possible starting lineup:.

Chapman; Fraser, Gogic, Jackson; Ramsay, Phillips, Taylor, John; Ramos, Young, Kabia.

The division's highest scorers come up against its least productive attack this weekend, and we expect that gulf in quality to be reflected at Celtic Park.

Celtic should have enough to secure a second consecutive league victory, extending their lead over St Mirren and maintaining at least a four-point cushion over Rangers heading into the following weekend.

Norwich City team news and predicted XI to face Cardiff City as key man Kenny McLean returns to full fitness

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (586 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Norwich City face off against Cardiff City off the back of a fantastic recent run of results, having won their last four games, scoring 15 goals in the process.
  • It has been revealed that A revitalised NCFC will be looking to continue their march up the Championship table towards the play-off positions.
  • The visit of an inconsistent Cardiff City side presents a good opportunity to pick up three more points.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Norwich City face off against Cardiff City off the back of a fantastic recent run of results, having won their last four games, scoring 15 goals in the process.

It has been revealed that A revitalised NCFC will be looking to continue their march up the Championship table towards the play-off positions. The Canaries now sit 12th in the table with 21 points from 15 matches, three points off the top eight.

The visit of an inconsistent Cardiff City side presents a good opportunity to pick up three more points.

Brian Barry-Murphy‘s side head eastwards after two extraordinary home matches: a 3-3 draw against West Ham, where the Welsh outfit let slip a three-goal lead, before coming back from three goals down themselves to beat Burnley 5-4 last time out.

Norwich City have a number of longer term absentees.

Ali Ahmed and Mohamed Toure remain injured. Having ruptured his ACL in pre-season, Ahmed will remain unavailable for the majority of the campaign and possibly longer, while Toure will return sooner and could be involved by the start of the Latest Year after his shoulder injury.

Having been out for about a month, Papa Amadou Diallo’s muscle injury will continue to keep him out of contention.

In a substantial boost though, key midfielder Kenny McLean has used the international window to regain fitness and will now be at Clement’s disposal against Cardiff City.

Grimshaw; Stacey, Darling, McConville, Chrisene; Field, Wright; Brooks, Maghoma, Musaba; Kvistgaarden.

With no upcoming injury concerns facing Clement’s side, the Norwich City team will likely remain unchanged after thrashing Bristol City in their last outing.

Industry observers note that dan Grimshaw keeps his place in goal with Vladan Kovacevic on the bench. The defence has been leaky at times this campaign, but after two clean sheets on the bounce, the NCFC boss will feel confident in maintaining the current backline.

The central midfield two of Jacob Wright and Sam Field have started the last three games together, and the standard of their performances means they are set to get the nod ahead of Pelle Mattsson and returning captain McLean. Paris Maghoma will keep his spot in the advanced midfield position, having netted four goals in as many games.

Industry observers note that on the wings, Andre Brooks will play on the right having started every league game thus far. Anthony Musaba is set to hold down his place on the left after three consecutive starts, yielding two goals and an assist.

Industry observers note that mathias Kvistgaarden is the preferred starter over Makama, so expect the Dane to lead the line. Makama has two goals off the bench in his last two games, as well as earning his first England U21 cap during the international window, so he will be pushing for that starting place.

Manchester City found guilty of 114 charges

📅 25 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (2094 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Manchester City have been found guilty of 114 of the 115 charges brought by the Premier League over breaches of its financial rules.
  • Sources indicate that city face a range of sanctions from a fine to points deductions and even expulsion from the Premier League.
  • If the verdict is upheld, with City expected to appeal, it will also raise question marks over the 20 trophies the club have won under Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan, whose Abu Dhabi group took over in 2008.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester City have been found guilty of 114 of the 115 charges brought by the Premier League over breaches of its financial rules. It is a decision that, if upheld, would equate to one of the biggest scandals in football history.

Sources indicate that city face a range of sanctions from a fine to points deductions and even expulsion from the Premier League. Or a combination of all, under rule W51 of its handbook. No punishment has yet been confirmed.

If the verdict is upheld, with City expected to appeal, it will also raise question marks over the 20 trophies the club have won under Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan, whose Abu Dhabi group took over in 2008.

It has been revealed that the charges can be broken down into five categories and relate to a period from 2009-23 in which City won six League Cups, three FA Cups, seven league titles and the Champions League. There is the provision for removing past titles, but that would appear remote.

City have been the dominant force in English football for most of that time, but that status is under threat with a verdict that will send shockwaves around Europe and could have huge ramifications for the club.

That is unless they can win an appeal, with sources cautioning it still may take up to another two to three years for the case to be resolved, following on from an already five-year investigation.

The Premier League’s rules provide for an independent appeal board with broad powers, including the ability to uphold, vary or overturn the independent commission’s decision.

In a recent development, it would therefore appear that despite the verdict, the case is far from being resolved and punishment decided. The details of the commission’s findings, when published, will be crucial to determining what happens next.

But if it is upheld, the verdict also opens up the possibility of City facing legal action from other clubs who feel they missed out on trophies and even merit money from league placings.

It is understood Premier League clubs are already discussing legal action and possible compensation claims as a result of the guilty verdict.

Each of those cases would have to be held individually, potentially leading to years more of litigation. Conversely, if City win their appeal, they too could take legal action against the Premier League the damage caused to their reputation.

There has not yet been an official confirmation of the independent panel’s verdict from the Premier League. The Premier League declined to comment.

Sources indicate that however, several sources have told Telegraph Sport that the panel has found City guilty of all but one of the charges they faced. The one that has not been proved is noted to be one of the most serious of the 115.

The damning verdict for City is a major newly introduced test of fragile UK relations with the United Arab Emirates, with whom bilateral trade was worth £25bn last year. Redacted freedom of information documents, seen by Telegraph Sport, show Abu Dhabi hosted UK government officials including Lord Stockwood, then investment minister, as recently as February. Khaldoon Al Mubarak, the City chairman and trusted adviser to the UAE president, was present at the meeting. Government notes from the meeting recorded that he “noted they are very proud of what they have achieved through their investments in Manchester”.

According to recent reports, the Government previously caused acrimony among senior leaders in Abu Dhabi after putting forward legislation to ban foreign states from owning UK newspapers and news magazines. The intervention prompted the collapse of a takeover of The Telegraph in April 2024, which was largely funded by Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan, the owner of City and vice-president and deputy prime minister of the United Arab Emirates.

The previous UK government has admitted its embassy in Abu Dhabi and the Foreign Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO) in London discussed the charges levelled at City by the Premier League. However it refused to disclose the correspondence.

Recent findings suggest that city have steadfastly maintained they are innocent, promising “irrefutable” evidence in support of their position, and had assembled some of the most expensive lawyers in the country to argue their case. Despite the verdict, the club are understood to be confident that it will win the argument in the end. Senior figures are remarked to be calm about the latest development, as significant as it seems.

Recent findings suggest that city rebuilt their team this summer and it is understood that signings were brought in on conventional player contracts, rather than terms including clauses triggered in the event of a heavy punishment. Given the club have consistently denied breaching financial regulations, and their deals for fresh players to work with head coach Enzo Maresca underlines their position.

Industry observers note that on Friday, a City spokesman stated: “The Premier League process remains ongoing, with significant elements to be completed, and subject to strict confidentiality. As such, Manchester City FC’s position remains consistent with the club’s statement of February 2023.

“The club have diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis that the Premier League board and executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence.”.

Sources close to Pep Guardiola, the former City manager who stepped down last summer after 10 years of remarkable success at the club, including a treble triumph in 2023 and an unprecedented fourth straight league title in 2024, insist he has not been informed of any verdict.

In the days after City were first charged, Guardiola mounted a fierce defence of the club, claiming: “I am fully convinced we will be [proved] innocent.”.

The verdict vindicates the Premier League’s decision to launch an investigation after explosive allegations that City had routinely broken financial rules were first made in Der Spiegel in 2018 based on the Football Leaks documents.

Uefa previously accused City of breaches of its financial regulations and announced in 2020 that it was suspending the club from the Champions League for two years for “overstating” sponsorship revenue between 2012 and 2016.

Recent findings suggest that city denied the Uefa charges and, after an appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport, the two-year ban was overturned. Cas found that a number of the claims brought by Uefa had fallen outside a five-year “time bar” and others were “not established”.

It did, however, still impose a €10m fine after ruling that City failed to cooperate with investigators. City had previously also agreed a settlement with Uefa of €20m in 2014 following an investigation into their finances.

Sources indicate that legal experts agreed that the commission’s verdict is far from the end of the case. Yasin Patel, barrister at Church Court Chambers, stated: “City’s lawyers will now analyse this decision and look at the options open to them to appeal, which may include procedural impropriety, wrongful interpretation of law, and legal errors – importantly, they can guarantee an appeal.

It has been revealed that “Sanctions could include a major fine, points deduction, relegation or even all three. Factoring in whether titles and trophies should be stripped, whether other clubs have been robbed of further revenue and opportunities due to City’s wrongdoings and losses incurred, we safely say that this is only the first chapter of a long-running legal saga that will not end any time soon.”.

Ian Hargreaves, partner with specialist disputes firm Quillon Law, said the verdict was “not the end of the story but the beginning of a new phase”, and added: “There is also the question of whether the panel’s decision can withstand a hard-fought appeal, and on what grounds any challenge might be brought. Much will depend on the detail of the panel’s findings and reasoning, which will inevitably be closely scrutinised by both sides.”.

Former Manchester City midfielder Rodri, who won the Ballon d’Or during his trophy-laden spell at the club, noted he believed the club were innocent.

According to recent reports, “For the players, it’s different than it is for journalists. I can understand all opinions, but we try to stay positive,” the Spain midfielder said while on international duty.

“When you see all the people who worked hard at City to achieve success, you know what we achieved can’t be taken away. It wasn’t paid for with money, but with effort and teamwork. Everything we achieved was deserved; we marked one of the great eras of English football. I believe in the club’s innocence – we already went through this in 2020.”.

Andy Burnham, the Prime Minister, said: “I think we would all need to study the independent commission’s report in some considerable detail before reaching any conclusions.”.

Zohran Kwame Mamdani, the mayor of Upcoming York, posted “114” in relation to the charges while former Manchester United players David de Gea and Rio Ferdinand both asked whether they should be due winner’s medals from past seasons.

The Premier League statement in February 2023 remarked that “a number of alleged breaches” had been referred to an independent commission. It then detailed each specific rule against each season in which the alleged breach took place. The precise number was not clear from the statement and led to varying reports between 115 and 130. Friday’s news suggested the figure was 115.

All the way to 2009-10, the first full season following the club’s takeover by Sheikh Mansour, who is a member of the Abu Dhabi Royal family and the vice president of the United Arab Emirates. There were charges relating to all 14 seasons until the Premier League completed their investigation during the 2022-23 campaign. In that time, City won seven Premier League titles, six League Cups, three FA Cups and the Champions League. They have since won another league title – the first club to do so four times in a row – as well as the Uefa Super Cup, the Fifa Club World Cup and the FA Cup and League Cup double last season.

They can be split into five groups. The biggest relates to the seasons from 2009-10 until 2017-18 and the requirement for clubs to provide accurate financial information and act in the utmost good faith.

The next set of rules concern the full disclosure of manager and player payments. The alleged manager breaches related to the period between 2009-10 and 2012-13, when Roberto Mancini was leading the team. The alleged breaches with respect to player payments relate to all of the seasons between 2010-11 and 2015-16.

Sources indicate that as well as providing financial detail, clubs were required to meet Uefa and Premier League rules which were designed to bring a club’s spending broadly in line with their income by placing set limits on losses. City were charged with breaches of Uefa’s licencing and financial fair play rules from 2013-14 until 2017-18, and the Premier League’s profit and sustainability rules from 2015-16 until 2017-18.

The final set of charges spanned the five seasons during which City were being investigated by the Premier League and rules that require members to cooperate in the utmost good faith by providing information and documents.

A full picture will only emerge when the commission publishes its findings but we know that the Premier League investigation began in December 2018 following allegations in the German newspaper Der Spiegel based on the Football Leaks documents. These included alleged payments to former manager Mancini for consultancy work at an Abu Dhabi-based club that was separate to his regular contract at City.

We also know that City were alleged to have breached rules over setting out image rights payments to players in their club contract. Der Spiegel reported that the Premier League investigation also focused on payments to under-age players, as well as whether club sponsors were paying for commercial deals themselves or a significant proportion was in fact effectively coming from owner Sheikh Mansour.

Sources indicate that city have always denied breaking any rules. In response to the Premier League statement about the alleged breaches, they remarked that they have “irrefutable evidence” to support their position and “look forward to this matter being put to rest once and for all.”.

According to recent reports, at the start of the hearing in September 2024, Guardiola also said: “Wait for the independent panel. We believe we have not done anything wrong.”.

Industry observers note that of the Football Leaks documents, City remarked: “We will not be providing any comment on out-of-context materials. The attempt to damage the club’s reputation is organised and clear.”.

Birmingham City have been issued a warning involving Jay Stansfield ahead of their crucial away trip to Stoke City on Saturday afternoon by modern-day Championship goalscoring supremo, Charlie Austin.

Chris Davies' side had won six of their seven games between the final international breaks of 2026, with a 2-1 success against Swansea City at St. Andrew's @ Knighthead Park on November 7th sending them top ahead of Middlesbrough and the Potters on goal difference.

After finishing 10th in 2025/26, Davies oversaw a relatively quiet summer transfer window in comparison to the two previous years of his tenure, and such a decision has clearly paid off.

The main question concerning Blues right now is whether they have the capability to sustain their promotion challenge for the remaining 31 games, as well as how they seek to add further quality in the January transfer window.

Stansfield's exploits in B9 are often analysed due to the club-record fee Birmingham parted with to sign the forward on a seven-year contract from Fulham in August 2024.

The 23-year-old has received mixed reviews over time, largely down to a decrease in output despite his overall importance within Davies' setup never being questioned.

His brace last time out saw him surpass 50 goals in all competitions for Blues, and is one of several difference-makers on show in Saturday's game at the Bet365 Stadium.

Discussing the clash with Stoke, Austin stated: "The clubs that have been in those positions are wanting to get back. It's nice to see the usual names up there and performing.

According to recent reports, "We're having this conversation in November. The way the Championship is, give it the week before Christmas and you could be at the opposite end.

Sources indicate that "It's going to be a fascinating game," the former striker claimed. "The thing is with Birmingham, for me, they heavily rely on Jay Stansfield.

Sources indicate that "That's my only problem with Birmingham. If anything happens to him, they're in big trouble.".

Stansfield has been viewed as the figurehead of Knighthead's ambitious project at Birmingham, but many supporters are likely to disagree with Austin's claim on the England youth international.

In the past three seasons, the striker may have hit double-figures, emphasising his importance whilst also adjusting to his current 'number 10' role, but there certainly doesn't appear to be an over-reliance on his services anymore.

Blues fans, what do you make of Charlie Austin's verdict on Jay Stansfield? Is it fair? Comment below!

Birmingham have scored three or more goals in four of their last six encounters, with the goals very much shared around during that timeframe as the likes of Alex Cochrane, Max Bird, Liam Millar, Demarai Gray and August Priske have all netted as well as Stansfield.

Davies will be pleased with how well the attacker has led the line in the victories over Millwall and Swansea in Priske's absence, which, in itself, creates a selection headache ahead of the matchup with Mark Robins' side.

With Stoke and Birmingham level on points, even with 30 matches to play afterwards, the potential victors in North Staffordshire have the chance to use the game as a springboard for future success.

The Potters have only lost once since August, which came in a narrow 3-2 defeat to Middlesbrough on October 13th, although both of Blues' two defeats came on the road against Norwich City and Cardiff City.

Recent findings suggest that as Austin alluded to, a fascinating contest lies in wait with both squads strong in defence and possessing attacking flair. Davies will be hoping Stansfield continues his impressive form whatever role he is assigned, whilst also needing his 10 teammates to step up to the plate as they have so often done.

'He exudes football in every movement, and his rise to the top is unstoppable.'.

It was a proud international break for the Bellinghams before a ball was kicked in Madrid, with Jude's 21-year-old younger brother Jobe also earning his first England call-up last week.

Jude and Jobe would have become the first brothers to play for England since Gary and Phil Neville 17 years ago, but the younger sibling stayed on Thomas Tuchel's bench as an unused substitute.

England, who topped Group C on goal difference over Spain, will now not play until the Nations League quarter-finals kick off next spring.

The final, should Tuchel's Three Lions make it that far, are scheduled for the summer.
