Tech Report: Huddersfield Town & Notts County are cringing at the same thing right now

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (988 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Tom Iorpenda was one of the EFL's brightest talents last season while at Notts County, but the 21-year-old has yet to see the pitch in any competition so far this year.
  • The former Brighton and Huddersfield Town academy product ended a five-year association with the Terriers this past summer, signing for Swansea City for around £1 million towards the end of the transfer window.
  • Iorpenda had played every game in league and play-off action for Notts in their League Two promotion campaign while on loan from Huddersfield last term, and returned to the Accu Stadium with plenty of momentum and a possible route into first-team action.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tom Iorpenda was one of the EFL's brightest talents last season while at Notts County, but the 21-year-old has yet to see the pitch in any competition so far this year.

The former Brighton and Huddersfield Town academy product ended a five-year association with the Terriers this past summer, signing for Swansea City for around £1 million towards the end of the transfer window.

Iorpenda had played every game in league and play-off action for Notts in their League Two promotion campaign while on loan from Huddersfield last term, and returned to the Accu Stadium with plenty of momentum and a possible route into first-team action.

In the end, with his contract up at the end of the season, Huddersfield opted to cash in on the versatile midfielder and insert a sell-on clause so they could profit further down the line, instead of possibly losing him for free.

It's safe to say it hasn't worked out yet at all, which must be a real frustration for the League One pair.

It's always difficult when a young star arrives at a club in the latter stages of the summer transfer window. Iorpenda spent the whole summer and pre-season with Huddersfield, signing for the Swans on August 30.

Swansea adopted a much more intense play style ahead of Vitor Matos' second season in charge in South Wales. They rank first in pressing sequences, high turnovers and have the lowest PPDA (passes per defensive action) in the Championship.

That's difficult to get up to speed with when you have a full pre-season, let alone when you don't.

Additionally, Iorpenda joined a Swansea side that, at the time, had won two and drawn one of their first three games and were about to make it three wins from four against Watford on September 1.

So, the 21-year-old arrived at the club with just two Championship appearances under his belt, totalling 50 minutes, from his time at Huddersfield, has had to get up to speed with their intensity and has been trying to dislodge what has been a winning lineup.

It's been difficult, and that's the reason why he still has no appearances so far in a Swansea shirt.

Industry observers note that iorpenda was everywhere for Notts last year. He predominantly played as an attacking midfielder, but Martin Paterson trusted him to man the engine room a bit further back, too, and as loan spells go, it was one of the best in the EFL last year.

Not only did Iorpenda start 46 of the 49 league and play-off games at Meadow Lane last season, but he also scored three and assisted eight, including setting up Jayden Luker (another loanee set for bigger things) for the only goal over two legs in the play-off semi-final against Chesterfield.

According to recent reports, per FotMob, he ranked in the top 3% of players in his position for defensive contributions, duels won and tackles, but also in the top 5% for touches, passes and fouls won. He operated mainly in the left channel, but he covered ground better than most could in League Two that year.

Recent findings suggest that notts County would have likely had Iorpenda right at the top of their summer wishlist after they secured promotion from League Two last season, no matter how unrealistic the signing appeared to be. He was ready to propel himself up the leagues, and perhaps the Magpies could have been entrusted to continue his development in the tier above.

How disappointing has it been to see Tom Iorpenda hardly play this season, Notts fans? Let us know in the comments.

Unfortunately, the 21-year-old's contract situation worked against them, and now they're being forced to see him ride the bench in the Championship.

Iorpenda's stock has fallen quite significantly since he joined Swansea, which doesn't bode well for a Huddersfield side who felt they could have been earning a little more than the £1m they pocketed in the original sale.

It's unknown what contract talks were held between the midfielder and Huddersfield over the summer, but from his lack of inclusion in any side under Martin Drury to start the season, it was clear he wasn't favoured.

Industry observers note that even the Terriers couldn't deny that he has potential, though, and a £1m + sell-on clause actually went down as a good deal for both sides. Swansea got a high-potential player for cheap, and Huddersfield banked a seven-figure fee for a guy they could have lost for nothing at the end of the season.

At the moment, though, they aren't getting any more than that base amount, as Iorpenda is yet to showcase any Championship quality just yet, mainly because he's had no chance to showcase anything.

Notts will be looking on, annoyed that their ex-loan star isn't enjoying life elsewhere, while the dreams of making some more money immediately from Huddersfield's side aren't coming to fruition, either.

It has been revealed that however, it's not as if Iorpenda has been left out of squads altogether. He's making the bench, just not getting on the pitch. In the 12 games he's been available for, he's made the 20-man squad in half of those.

He'll be one of the players looking to impress whoever the newhead coach turns out to be, after Vitor Matos left Swansea on Wednesday to take charge at Ligue 1 outfit Strasbourg.

A potential new playstyle could be implemented that benefits Iorpenda, or the new boss could simply come into the job with a fresh slate, and the ex-Huddersfield man won't already be battling with settled starters.

Either way, it may only be a matter of time before Iorpenda gets to see the pitch in a Swansea shirt for the first time, and those at Huddersfield and Notts County who have cringed at his involvement so far will hope he can make a name for himself when he does.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Sully | 19 Nov 2026 15:52, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 15:54.

Southampton will resume their Championship campaign with a home clash against Derby County on Saturday.

The Saints return from the international break in seventh spot, while the Rams are languishing in 23rd place in the Championship table.

Southampton enjoyed a fine run of form after returning from the September/October international break, recording four wins and two draws in a six-game unbeaten run.

However, their undefeated streak came to a disappointing end with a 1-0 away loss against basement side Preston North End in their final outing before the two-week break.

Tonda Eckert’s side failed to produce a response to Jordan Thompson’s 33rd-minute effort, as they drew a blank for the first time on the road this season.

Despite that result, the Saints are still firmly in the promotion battle, sitting in seventh spot and five points adrift of the automatic promotion places ahead of Saturday’s meeting with the Rams.

They head into that contest with the league’s best home record, having won six and drawn one of their seven Championship outings at St Mary’s this term, scoring 20 goals and conceding on just five occasions.

They have also won their last two home league games against Derby, including a hard-fought 2-1 victory in April’s encounter between the two sides.

While the Saints are targeting promotion, Derby are focusing on retaining their Championship status after winning just two of their 15 league matches (D4, L9).

They at least managed to end a 10-game winless run in their final outing before the international window, which saw them overturn a one-goal deficit to record a 3-1 victory over Bolton Wanderers.

Ryan Nyambe, Jack Robinson and Rhian Brewster all found the net in the second period to ease some of the heavy pressure on head coach John Eustace.

However, Eustace knows he needs a positive run of results if he is to prove he is the right manager to lead Derby out of their current predicament, with five points separating the Rams from safety.

Derby have failed to win any of their last five away games, but they have at least enjoyed success on the south coast this season, with September’s 2-0 win over Portsmouth representing their only win on the road this term.

If they are to claim the spoils on Saturday, the visitors will need to claim their first Championship win at St Mary’s since recording a 2-1 victory in the second leg of the 2006-07 playoff semi-finals.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 18:47 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 05:54 EST, 16 November 2026.

Mauricio Pochettino enjoyed a stellar penultimate game in charge of the United States, thrashing Haiti 6-0.

The newly appointed Manchester United manager has just one game left before sinking his teeth into the job at Old Trafford.

He will link up with United on Wednesday, but first must navigate the second leg of their Concacaf Nations League quarter-final tie with Haiti on Tuesday.

Here, Pochettino cut a fairly reserved figure on the touchline as he was rewarded for trusting youth - and even saw his team score from a corner, something United don't do much of these days.

Without further ado, here are four things Manchester United fans learned from the win.

Mauricio Pochettino, dressed in a scarf, was fairly reserved as the United States beat Haiti 6-0.

Pochettino’s arrival spells good news for United’s proud tradition of promoting homegrown youth - it is glad tidings for the likes of Shea Lacey and Kobbie Mainoo. You wonder if, for a while, JJ Gabriel will look on forlornly from Real Madrid’s reserves.

The Argentinian handed out 13 debuts in the September-October international break, including to eight teenagers in one 4-1 victory over Peru.

Recent findings suggest that his strategy was no different here as he started 18-year-old Julian Hall up front and Diego Kochen, 20, in goal - both players he has given debuts to this year. He was rewarded, with Hall scoring his fourth goal in just five games for the United States, while Kochen kept a clean sheet.

Despite his affinity for the stars of tomorrow, he is a hard schoolmaster. In a column for The Athletic in 2022, he revealed that he sat a young Harry Kane down for a brutal meeting where he indicated him stats and clips to justify why he wasn’t playing him more.

It has been revealed that pochettino had known Kane’s potential from their first training session but wanted the ‘tough conversation’ to get the best out of him. Kane went on to score 169 goals under him for Tottenham, and now he’s the best player in the world.

His trust in fresh faces could inject some much-needed enthusiasm around the club, strengthen the squad's connection with the fanbase, and increase the energy levels in one of the Premier League's oldest, most lethargic teams.

The likes of Shea Lacey will be delighted at how Pochettino puts trust in younger players.

Julian Hall, 18, struck his fourth goal in five games for the United States under Pochettino.

Pochettino has a history of getting the most out of attacking midfielders such as Dele Alli, Christian Eriksen, and Adam Lallana. You can add Cole Palmer to that list too, though he was primarily a right winger under him at Chelsea.

Manchester United desperately need him to get a tune out of Bruno Fernandes, who has cut a frustrated figure this season and whose creative efficiency has declined - though he still has nine goal involvements.

If Christian Pulisic’s performance against Haiti is anything to go by, Fernandes will be happy. The attacking midfielder scored twice, playing a free role and being given penalty duty.

In a recent development, the 28-year-old was also asked to muck in defensively, and that’s something Fernandes is willing to do. Across the seasons, he has often covered more ground than any of his team-mates.

Recent findings suggest that pochettino and Pulisic have seemingly had a distant relationship, despite the latter’s insistence to the contrary. The manager branded it ‘b*******’ when the AC Milan star opted out of the Gold Cup last year, and left him out of his selection a couple of months ago, bringing in 16-year-old Cavan Sullivan.

Asked about Pochettino's upcoming final game, Pulisic remarked at full-time: 'We're treating it like any other game.' No emotion on display.

Depending on how you interpret Fernandes - either a die-for-the-badge club servant or a primadonna - Pochettino could draw the best or worst out of the Portuguese.

Pochettino often gets the best out of attacking midfielders - will he work well with Bruno Fernandes?

He has had a distant relationship with Christian Pulisic, but the AC Milan star scored twice here.

Pochettino tends to push his defensive lines high up the pitch and his strategy with the United States has been no different.

They were almost caught out for trying to play the offside trap early on as a simple ball from midfield sent Danley Jean Jacques through one-on-one, forcing Kochen into a good save.

Meanwhile, full-backs Antonee Robinson and Alex Freeman were constantly pushing high and overlapping in his 4-2-3-1 system - although you’d obviously expect a strong level of intent when they’re favourites against Haiti.

Given his high-line tradition, Pochettino may well favour more mobile defenders such as Leny Yoro and Patrick Dorgu.

The battle for Harry Maguire will be to convince his fresh boss that his other qualities compensate for his lack of pace.

Pochettino takes inspiration from the frenetic football of Marcelo Bielsa, who managed him at Newell’s Old Boys in Argentina.

But he'll have to balance his philosophy with the reality of United's woeful defensive record this campaign. Just the 15 goals conceded in the last five games...

Pochettino demonstrated an eagerness to intervene early in the game - a possible boost after Michael Carrick suffered from slow starts.

Pochettino is typically seen as an animated character on the touchline, in contrast to Carrick's statesmanlike behaviour, but he spent lots of time in his seat here.

He has calmed down somewhat these days - though he did kick a crate of bottles in frustration at the World Cup - and didn’t even react much when his team scored.

A major criticism of Carrick is that he takes too long to change things in-game, often going late with substitutions. Pochettino has traditionally leaned that way, too, but he was eager to influence proceedings here.

Even three minutes in, at a break while Antonee Robinson was being treated, he called Pulisic over for what looked like an intense tactical chat.

According to recent reports, united have been plagued by slow starts this season, so it was encouraging to see Pochettino so alert and full of ideas early into the game. He could have coasted, really, but wanted to eke out every advantage.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Championship is back after yet another international break, and we've now got a straight sprint until the Easter weekend with no interruptions.

The second-tier returns with a bang, as two of the sides sitting on 29 points atop the table go head-to-head at the bet365 Stadium on Saturday.

Industry observers note that stoke City, who have exceeded early-season expectations once more, will be keen not to fade away over the coming months like they did last year. A win at home against the current table-toppers, Birmingham City, would go a long way towards doing that.

It has been revealed that the Blues were ruthless over the seven-game block between international breaks, winning six of seven, and three of those wins came by at least a three-goal margin. Their form away from St Andrew's is as substantial a contributor to their place atop the table, winning just one game fewer already this year than they did in the entirety of last season.

Industry observers note that but only Swansea City and Middlesbrough — two fellow quick-starters — have come away from Stoke with all three points, and Kim Hellberg's side needed a late winner to do so. This won't be an easy matchup for either, and three points will give a massive boost to both sides' promotion hopes.

These five players, however, won't be able to feature.

French attacker Lamine Cisse had started six straight for Stoke before he went down inside 20 minutes against Bristol City last month and was forced off.

The extended run in the team, plus a goal in the win at Bolton Wanderers, gave hope that the £2m arrival last summer from Bastia was starting to find his feet in Mark Robins' side, so this setback is especially frustrating.

The ankle injury he picked up should see him out until Christmas.

Ato Ampah has had a terrible time with injuries ever since he arrived at Stoke from Chelsea's academy back in January.

Recent findings suggest that he's yet to make his debut for the Potters due to a series of setbacks. Last season, it was an elongated recovery from a toe injury which kept him on the sidelines, and over pre-season he suffered a setback to that recovery.

While spending time with the Under-21s, though, the 20-year-old picked up an impact injury to his knee, which required surgery and will keep him out for the foreseeable future.

Recent findings suggest that it's still unconfirmed whether Eric Bocat will be able to return against Birmingham. He's missed the last four games with a knee injury, which forced him off against Derby County last month.

The hope after his diagnosis was that the left-back could make his return after the international break, but he remains a doubt, with Ben Johnson and Luca Bombino waiting in the wings to deputise in his absence.

Fellow left-back Aaron Cresswell is also a doubt for Saturday's clash with Birmingham, as he nears closer to a return to fitness from a knee injury he picked up in pre-season.

The 36-year-old remained a Stoke player over the summer, signing a one-year extension after he made 25 league appearances in his debut campaign following his departure from West Ham United.

According to recent reports, who do you think will come out on top between Stoke City and Birmingham City on Saturday? Let us know in the comments.

Birmingham's bill of health is relatively clear heading into the weekend. James Beadle and August Priske are both available again after missing a couple before the break, and Kristoffer Lund, who missed six weeks, is also back training.

Marc Leonard looked to be on his way out of Birmingham after heading on loan to Hearts back in January, but an Achilles injury suffered weeks before the end of the campaign saw him return to St Andrew's for treatment.

He'll remain out until the New Year, and all eyes will be on what his role in Chris Davies' side will be after his return.

  • Boro entered the final international break of the year having missed the opportunity to become league leaders, as a defeat to Wrexham was followed by a goalless draw away to Watford, while the Robins continued their slide down the table after suffering a humiliating 5-0 home defeat to Norwich City just under a fortnight ago.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Calum Burrowes | 19 Nov 2026 15:53, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 16:00.

Middlesbrough will be looking to move to the top of the Championship table this weekend when they welcome a struggling Bristol City side to the Riverside Stadium.

Boro entered the final international break of the year having missed the opportunity to become league leaders, as a defeat to Wrexham was followed by a goalless draw away to Watford, while the Robins continued their slide down the table after suffering a humiliating 5-0 home defeat to Norwich City just under a fortnight ago.

Kim Hellberg and his Middlesbrough side return to the Riverside Stadium for the first time since Halloween with an opportunity to leapfrog Birmingham City and move to the top of the Championship table.

The Blues have made an unexpected push for first place in recent weeks after winning three consecutive matches, while Boro managed just one victory, alongside a defeat and a draw, leaving both sides level on 29 points ahead of matchweek 16.

Such is the competitiveness of the Championship that Middlesbrough's tally of 29 points provides them with just a three-point cushion over sixth place, highlighting how promptly the standings can change.

Although their form at the start of November was somewhat inconsistent, Boro return to home soil where they are unbeaten in seven matches, collecting 17 points and scoring 17 goals during that run, with only Southampton boasting a better home record than Hellberg's side.

Last season saw Hellberg and his Middlesbrough team miss out on promotion to the Premier League following one of the most dramatic and controversial playoff campaigns in recent memory, despite occupying a place in the top two for much of the season.

Their success during the 2025-26 campaign was built on a prolific attack that scored 72 goals in 46 matches, a total bettered by just three teams, and they have once again impressed in the final third this season, with only one side scoring more than their 30 goals.

As for Bristol City, they entered the international break with serious questions surrounding the future of manager Michael Skubala after a dreadful run of form saw them fall out of the playoff places and down to 17th in the table.

Since the first international break ended in September, the Robins have won just one of their subsequent seven Championship matches and were widely tipped to part firm with the former Lincoln City boss during the past fortnight, but the club have opted to stick with him as he prepares to take charge of his 17th match on Saturday.

A short video published by the club last week showed CEO Charlie Boss confirming that they would "give Skubala the opportunity to turn around the home form", with Bristol City's two victories at Ashton Gate representing the fourth-worst record in the division and a stark contrast to that of their upcoming opponents.

The Robins enjoyed a productive seven-day spell in which they collected nine points from a possible nine against Portsmouth, Preston North End and Burnley, but have since suffered a series of disappointing results that have seen their playoff ambitions replaced by growing concerns over a potential relegation battle.

Norwich arrived in the South West in encouraging form, but few would have expected them to inflict such a heavy defeat on Skubala's side, with the 5-0 loss at Ashton Gate subsequently described by the manager as one of the most difficult afternoons of his career.

Although the Robins face one of the division's strongest sides this weekend, they can at least take confidence from their recent record against Boro, with the North Yorkshire outfit winless in their last nine league meetings and without a victory over Bristol City since August 2021.

Middlesbrough Championship form:.

Bristol City Championship form:.

Middlesbrough could name the same starting XI that drew with Watford almost a fortnight ago, although Hellberg may be tempted to make changes as his side look to return to winning ways.

Former Robins goalkeeper Radek Vitek is expected to retain his place between the posts, while former Bristol City players Tommy Conway, Neto Borges and Luke Ayling could all come into contention to face their old club after starting on the bench last time out.

Rokas Pusktas has suffered another injury setback after undergoing surgery on a hamstring problem and has managed just 12 minutes of football for Boro since joining from Hajduk Split in August.

Hellberg will also be without Alfie Jones, who remains sidelined with a calf injury, but could welcome the Championship's leading scorer back into the fold, with Will Lankshear looking to add to his 13 league goals, which have come at an impressive rate of one every 81 minutes.

Meanwhile, Bristol City are expected to have just one absentee for Saturday's trip north, with Noah Eile likely to miss out through illness.

Although their major injury crisis from last season is very much a thing of the past, the Robins have made several unexpected changes to their recent starting lineups, making it difficult to predict the team Skubala will select.

New goalkeeper Sam Tickle was dropped in favour of Brad Collins after just 11 appearances for his new club but could be reinstated after his replacement made several high-profile errors leading to goals during his four starts, conceding an average of 2.3 goals per game during that time.

Skubala has also alternated between a lone striker and a two-man forward partnership in recent weeks and could once again make changes as he looks to turn around his side's disappointing run of form.

Rio Cardines opted out of international duty with Trinidad and Tobago over the past fortnight after featuring in every one of the Robins' Championship matches during his debut season as a professional, and he is expected to return to the attack this weekend as he looks to build on the impressive six assists he has already provided.

Vitek; Brittain, Phillips, Malanda, Bryam; Berhalter, Morris, McGree; Conway, Strelec, Sarmiento.

Bristol City possible starting lineup:.

Tickle; Tanner, Dickie, Eissat, Pring; Williams, Randell; Cardines, Knight, Twine; Tolaj.

With one of the division's most out-of-form sides facing a team that has been exceptionally difficult to beat on home soil, we expect the result to go Middlesbrough's way.

Although the Robins boast an impressive recent record against Boro, we expect that run to come to an end on Saturday as Hellberg's side continue their push towards the top of the Championship table.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Thomas Tuchel has never been inclined to place much faith in the most famous right-back at his disposal, Trent Alexander-Arnold, once of Liverpool, now of Real Madrid, and – back in an England shirt – still capable of changing games in the blink of an eye.

England always looked likely to defeat a beleaguered Czech Republic team down to 10 men with just 25 minutes played, but it still required one man to conjure the moment of inspiration in this Nations League tie. This was the first cap in 15 months for the right-back now known simply as “Trent” in an England shirt – as well as his Real Madrid jersey – rather than the six syllables of his surname. With the game level at half-time, two minutes into the newly introduced half, he twice won the ball before landing a cross on the head of Anthony Gordon for the first goal.

TRENT ➡️ GORDON ⚽️🔥Anthony Gordon can't stop scoring for England, 3 goals in his last 3 games for England 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿#ITVFootball | @England pic.twitter.com/xmqPIULJ24.

Sources indicate that will the Alexander-Arnold with England experiment survive? One feels that Tuchel will need a little more to convince him to abandon whatever reservations he has about the Liverpudlian. A week short of his 28th birthday, Alexander-Arnold was winning just his 35th cap. His Real Madrid team-mate Jude Bellingham, a second-half substitute, was earning his 58th cap less than two months after his 23rd birthday. Bellingham was on as captain in place of the man he replaced, Harry Kane, scorer of England’s second. Bellingham’s international career has taken a much less rocky path than that of his Real team-mate.

According to recent reports, having missed the World Cup finals this summer, and had little good fortune around previous tournaments, one wonders if Euro 2028 might be the watershed moment for Alexander-Arnold. Either way, against opponents who sit back, he is lethal when it is time for the substantial delivery. Alexander-Arnold may not have the breadth of England experience that some of his peers have accumulated, but he does have plenty of experience of big games.

“I make that run time and time again,” Gordon mentioned of his anticipation of the Alexander-Arnold cross, “but only a set number of players have that ability, that technique and the bravery to risk a mistake to play that pass. And that’s why I have been dying to play with him [Alexander-Arnold]. He’s been on his own journey but has trained really well this week. He should have played more. Sorry – he would have loved to have played more.”.

Sources indicate that A Freudian slip from the Barcelona winger, another Liverpudlian in Spain, who himself has barely put a foot wrong for England of late. He has three goals in three games for England, including the World Cup semi-final against Argentina. This was an England team that Tuchel fine-tuned, first to give a rest to Bellingham and in other quarters, too. Lewis Hall started at left-back. Trevoh Chalobah won his third England cap at centre-back. Alex Scott, of Bournemouth, was given his debut off the bench in the second half and Rio Ngumoha won the second cap of his England career, just one month after his 18th birthday.

As for Kane, his 87th goal for England now puts him within two goals of Robert Lewandowski, among four greats in the seven ahead of Kane on the all-time international goalscorers’ list. By the end of this international break the England captain should have equalled Peter Shilton’s record 125 caps. It has been an astonishing career even if it ends tomorrow. Following the missed penalty against Spain, Kane was again the man in the right place at the right time when Morgan Rogers’s shot was blocked in the second half.

Recent findings suggest that “Strange to get an early red card,” Tuchel stated. “Not the best for the team and spectators. It’s an awkward one, but we kept going, got a win and that’s what counts.” Not quite a vintage Czech Republic team, either, and when their best player of the opening stages, the attacking midfielder Pavel Sulc, of Lyon in Ligue 1, was dismissed after 25 minutes, it certainly did not become any easier for the home team. Sulc, the Czech player of the year in 2025, had mistimed a tackle on Elliot Anderson, which on a VAR review, the Turkish referee Umut Meler decided was worthy of an upgrade from yellow to red. It was high on the right calf of the England midfielder.

In a recent development, czech Republic DOWN TO 10 MEN! 🟥Pavel Šulc sees red for a dangerous challenge on Elliot Anderson#ITVFootball | @England pic.twitter.com/B2YOLuS0vL.

England had looked once more a little open to the counter-attack in the early stages, with Sulc one notable runner. This was not an opponent of the quality of Spain and Tuchel’s players were able to recover the situation. When they lose the ball in the opposition’s half, England tend to look vulnerable.

It has been revealed that even before the red card Rogers had hit a post. Myles Lewis-Skelly, playing in midfield, was booked for a foul on Lukas Serv and was pursued thereafter by the Czech players hoping to get an upgrade on the yellow card. He was substituted at half-time, with Eberechi Eze on in his place.

Recent findings suggest that “I spoke to Ant [Gordon] at half-time,” Alexander-Arnold said later to ITV, “and I said if I’m getting in those spaces make sure you get to the back post. You don’t expect to get it that fast, but it did and it worked.”.

Two minutes after the break, Alexander-Arnold suddenly burst into life. He won the ball back in his own area and then drove forward in search of the return. When that did not come, he raced back to win the ball again and unleashed one of those right-footed outswingers to the back post, where Gordon guided in the header. “Really proud to score that,” Gordon said, “because I can’t tell you the number of hours I’ve spent practising headers.”.

In a recent development, kane scored the second just a minute before he was replaced and Bellingham took the captain’s armband and the role as a No 9. One day someone will have to step into those goalscorer’s boots on a permanent basis and try to replace Kane – although it may be a while yet.

Thomas Tuchel has backed Jude Bellingham as a future England captain after giving him the armband in the victory over the Czech Republic.

In the absence of Declan Rice, who was vice-captain at the World Cup, Bellingham assumed the role when he came on for Harry Kane, who is now in his 10th season as England captain and also scored in the 2-0 win in Prague.

The Professional Footballers’ Association has leapt to Cole Palmer’s defence following his withdrawal from the England squad.

The union’s CEO,  Maheta Molango, said the Chelsea forward is a victim of a “sick” system that is demanding too much from players physically.

“When England see five players who need to withdraw when the single most proud moment a player has is to be called up for the national team, you just ask yourself, what’s wrong about the industry?” Molango mentioned at the Fifpro performance summit in London.

“You see people like Cole Palmer, someone who would have played four consecutive summers in a row had he gone to the World Cup, and you wonder why is he missing?”He’s missing because he’s a victim of the calendar and that’s something that needs to absolutely trigger the alarm bells.”.

Man City used ‘sham’ sponsorships in £830m cheating scheme.

Manchester City arranged “sham” sponsorships in a near-£1bn plot to flout Premier League rules, an independent commission has found.

It was confirmed on Tuesday that City had been found guilty of all charges related to “serious breaches” of the league’s financial rules, with the commission also upholding all but one in relation to their failure to co-operate with an investigation spanning over three years.

The commission found that, of £949.94m City claimed in commercial income over a nine-year period, only £119.25m was legitimate, with the remaining £830.69m illicitly paid by their Abu Dhabi owners.

In a recent development, good evening and welcome to live coverage of the Uefa Nations League match between Czech Republic and England from Slavia Prague’s Eden Stadium. The home side, 49th in the Fifa rankings, scrambled their way to World Cup qualification with victories in the play-offs in penalty shoot-outs over Ireland and Denmark, promptly stank Group A out in Mexico/Canada/United States, drawing with South Africa but losing to South Korea and Mexico to finish last.

Miroslav Koubek, their 74-year-old manager, the oldest in the competition’s history, promptly stood down and has been replaced by their first foreign head coach, Santi, the former Atlético Madrid centre-half, who spent 15 years moving from managing Spain’s U17s, to the U19s and then the U21s. Little wonder, given his CV, that he is looking to refresh his squad with a transfusion of young players, a requirement made all the more urgent by the international retirement of stalwart centre-forward Patrick Schick and the absence of West Ham’s Tomas Soucek who damaged his ankle in that 3-0 defeat by Mexico on June 25 and has not kicked a ball since.

By Oliver Thomas | 19 Nov 2026 16:00, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 20:24.

Chelsea will be looking to return to winning ways and strengthen their top-four credentials when they take on Leeds United in Saturday afternoon’s Premier League contest at Stamford Bridge.

These two teams served up a nine-goal thriller in the EFL Cup just a couple of months ago, with the West Londoners securing a 6-3 comeback victory in the third round.

Chelsea entered the international break on a sour note with just one win and three defeats to their name in all competitions, crashing out of the EFL Cup to Liverpool and enduring two setbacks in the Premier League.

The Blues responded to a surprise 2-0 home loss to Spurs by beating Man United at Stamford Bridge by the same scoreline, but they came back down to earth a fortnight ago with a disappointing 1-0 defeat to basement club Sunderland at the Stadium of Light.

Sources indicate that five wins, one draw and four defeats have been posted in Xabi Alonso’s first 10 top-flight games for Chelsea, who sit fifth in the Premier League table and just two points behind Liverpool in fourth. However, Aston Villa down in 10th spot are only three points adrift of the Blues.

Having lost three of their first five PL away games for the first time since 2015-16 under Jose Mourinho, Chelsea should welcome this weekend’s return to Stamford Bridge where they have accumulated 10 of their 16 top-flight points this term, scoring the second-most home goals in the division (13).

The West Londoners have also won eight of their last 10 home battles with Leeds across all tournaments (D2) since a 2-0 defeat back in December 1999, though they were held to a 2-2 draw in this exact league fixture last season after letting a two-goal lead slip in the second half.

Following a five-match winless run that placed Daniel Farke under growing pressure, Leeds secured a much-needed 1-0 victory over Tottenham Hotspur at Elland Road to enter the international break on a high.

A dominant second-half display was rewarded with a late strike from substitute Noah Okafor to help Leeds claim their third Premier League win of the season and rise to ninth in the table, six points clear of the bottom three and just two points behind Saturday’s opponents Chelsea in fifth.

Leeds are unbeaten across their last nine Premier League home matches (W5 D4) – their longest run at Elland Road in the top flight since an impressive 15-match streak between January and December 2001 – but they have only won one of their last eight league games on the road (D4 L3).

The Whites are now gearing up for four tricky away trips to Chelsea, Man City, Liverpool and Aston Villa, with Farke hoping that his side can showcase the same relentless character, commitment and unity shown in their win over Spurs as they attempt to improve their fortunes away from home.

In a recent development, leeds head into this weekend’s contest seeking to end a 10-game winless run away against Chelsea in all competitions (D2 L8). However, having avoided defeat in their last two league meetings (3-1 at home, 2-2 away), the Whites will aim to go three consecutive games unbeaten against the Blues for the first time since between November 2000 and October 2001.

Chelsea’s Reece James (knee), Maxence Lacroix (hamstring) and Jamie Gittens (ankle) all remain sidelined with injuries, but there is hope that Joao Pedro could be ready to return after missing the last four matches with a thigh problem.

Moises Caicedo (illness), Jorrel Hato (back) and Josh Acheampong (unspecified) are all doubtful, but goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez should be ready to start ahead for Mike Penders after recovering from a broken jaw to represent Argentina during the international break.

It has been revealed that morgan Rogers provided four second-half assists in the aforementioned EFL Cup win over Leeds in September, while Cole Palmer and Danny Welbeck both netted a brace. However, Welbeck may have to settle for a place on the bench once again, with Alonso possibly favouring either Estevao Willian or Pedro Neto in a central role alongside Rogers and Palmer.

As for Leeds, young forward Mateo Joseph is making positive progress in his recovery from a serious knee injury, but he remains sidelined, while midfielder Anton Stach is doubtful after missing the win over Spurs with a broken toe.

Farke will consider sticking with a two-man frontline of Dominic Calvert-Lewin and Lukas Nmecha, with Sean Longstaff and Ao Tanaka linking up with ex-Chelsea youngster Ethan Ampadu in midfield.

However, Noah Okafor will hope to force his way into the first XI after scoring as a substitute against Spurs, while Harry Wilson, Brendan Aaronson and Joe Rodon are also contenders to earn a recall, the latter of whom recently recovered from a long-term injury.

Chelsea have not been the same prolific outfit without the presence of Joao Pedro up front, and they could find it difficult to break down a robust Leeds backline without a natural focal point.

Despite only one of the Blues' last six Premier League matches seeing both teams score, we can see the net rippling at both ends on this occasion, with the hosts bouncing back from recent setbacks and edging to a slender victory.

The Championship returns this weekend after the November international break, and at Molineux, Wolves look to extend their unbeaten league run to seven against Charlton Athletic.

The Addicks picked up a much-needed 2-1 win over Sheffield United at the Valley in the final game before the break, snapping an 11-game winless streak and alleviating some of the pressure that may have been building on Nathan Jones.

Now the next task is to replicate that on the road, where they've failed to win since their first away game of the season against West Ham United, but it won't be easy against a Wolves side who are within touching distance of top spot.

There are still parts of the Old Gold fanbase who are sceptical of head coach Cesar Peixoto, but one thing they can agree on is that, Bolton Wanderers aside, they've been well in control of their home games this season.

Both sides will be keen to take all three points, but these eight players won't be available to help do so.

The key injury in the Wolves camp remains with Raul Jimenez, with the veteran striker set to miss the rest of the calendar year after going in for knee surgery in mid-October.

The 35-year-old rejoined the club this past summer after three years at Fulham, where he still showcased his Premier League goalscoring qualities, netting 28 league goals in those three seasons.

He scored three in his first six back at Molineux, but isn't close to being able to add to that.

Left-back Ghislain Konan was brought to Wolves in the summer from Gil Vicente, reuniting with Cesar Peixoto in the first place. The 30-year-old provided some much-needed experience, with 59 Ivorian caps throughout his career.

However, Konan hasn't gotten going in the Old Gold just yet, and after just three appearances, he was sidelined until late December after picking up an MCL injury.

Charlton boss Nathan Jones was as coy as ever when discussing injuries ahead of the trip to Wolves, stating that those who missed Sheffield United are "closer than they were two weeks ago," and instead putting the focus on those who came in to replace those injured players.

Club captain Lloyd Jones was absent from a league squad for the first time this season against the Blades. He'd played every minute up until then. The hip injury he picked up could see him back this weekend, but he remains a doubt.

Karlarn Grant has also been a key part of Nathan Jones' side since making his return to the side he came through the academy with this past summer.

He was also absent from a league squad for the first time this season with a back problem last time out.

Nathaniel Chalobah was the third absentee from that win over Sheffield United after picking up a thigh injury.

It's the latest setback in what has been a troubling few years for the 31-year-old. He's already missed two months of the current season with a similar matter, and only played just over 1,000 minutes of league action across two years at Sheffield Wednesday prior to his summer move to the Valley, due to injury, too.

Sources indicate that reece Burke is another in the Charlton squad who has battled injury problems throughout his career. He reunited with ex-Luton Town boss Jones ahead of last season, having played fewer than 27 league games per year in his four campaigns with the Hatters.

He only managed 17 appearances last season and has yet to see the pitch this year after suffering an innocuous injury ahead of an EFL Cup match with Tottenham Hotspur back in August.

Sources indicate that charlton are more transparent with their long-term setbacks. Rob Apter is one of those, with a knee injury picked up a month ago, sidelining him for "an extended spell.".

Who do you think will pick up all three points on Saturday? Let us know in the comments.

The Scotsman was on the fringes anyway, with just 11 Championship minutes under his belt. The former Blackpool man spent the latter stages of last season on loan at Bolton.

Kenyan centre-back Collins Sichenje will miss the remainder of the campaign after he suffered an ACL injury during that aforementioned EFL Cup tie at Tottenham back in August.

The 23-year-old has only made 10 appearances since his mid-season move from Vojvodina last term.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Lille will be looking to strengthen their position in the Ligue 1 title race when they welcome Lyon to the Stade Pierre-Mauroy on Saturday evening for matchday 11 action.
  • The hosts sit second in the Ligue 1 table with 21 points from their opening 10 matches, two behind leaders Paris Saint-Germain, while the fifth-placed visitors have 17 points and will be hoping to close the gap on their opponents in Carlos Vicens's first game in charge.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Adeyeye Oluwapelumi | 19 Nov 2026 16:04, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 20:37.

Lille will be looking to strengthen their position in the Ligue 1 title race when they welcome Lyon to the Stade Pierre-Mauroy on Saturday evening for matchday 11 action.

The hosts sit second in the Ligue 1 table with 21 points from their opening 10 matches, two behind leaders Paris Saint-Germain, while the fifth-placed visitors have 17 points and will be hoping to close the gap on their opponents in Carlos Vicens's first game in charge.

Lille head into the weekend in encouraging form after winning their last two league outings, beating Lens 1-0 before claiming a 2-1 victory away to Rennes prior to the international break, where Nathan Ngoy's second-half goal proved decisive.

Davide Ancelotti will be particularly pleased with how his side have rediscovered their rhythm after consecutive draws against Brest and Monaco derailed the Mastiffs' title charge, with the northern French outfit having lost just once in their opening 10 Ligue 1 fixtures (W6, D3).

Much of Lille's success this season has been built on their defensive solidity, with seven goals conceded representing the best record in the division, while five clean sheets leave them behind only Lorient (six) in that regard.

Les Dogues have also found the net in every league outing this season, although they have scored more than once in just 40% of their 10 top-flight matches, including two of their five fixtures on their own turf.

Nevertheless, Lille have been reliable at the Stade Pierre-Mauroy, winning three of their five Ligue 1 games at the ground and avoiding defeat in the other two to boast the division's fifth-best home record.

Victory on Saturday would not only strengthen the hosts' position in the standings but also provide a timely confidence boost ahead of Wednesday's Champions League meeting with Bayern Munich, with the Mastiffs presently second from bottom in the league phase table after collecting just one point from their opening four continental fixtures.

Vicens will also have one eye on next Thursday’s home meeting with Lillstrom in the Europa League, where Lyon sit 13th in the 36-team table after picking up seven points from their first four matches.

However, the Spanish coach's immediate priority will be to get his upcoming side back to winning ways following a 2-0 defeat at Brest in Lyon's most recent league outing, which came under interim boss Jorge Maciel following the departure of Paolo Fonseca for Sporting Lisbon.

That setback further highlighted Lyon's struggles on the road, having now lost their last three Ligue 1 away matches while conceding exactly two goals in each of those outings, with their only victory in five domestic trips this season coming against Toulouse on the opening weekend.

Nevertheless, a superior head-to-head record should offer the visitors some encouragement ahead of Saturday's contest, considering Lyon have won six of their last seven meetings across all competitions (D1) with Lille, including 1-0 victories in both league encounters last season.

Lille remain without Tiago Santos, who is expected to miss the remainder of the season after rupturing his cruciate ligament, while Hamza Igamane is also unavailable as he continues his recovery from an ACL injury, although a return is expected in December.

Ayase Ueda is doubtful after sustaining a plantar fascia injury, with the forward having resumed running but yet to return to full training, although Ancelotti previously suggested that the Japanese attacker could be available for this fixture.

Hakon Arnar Haraldsson has operated as a makeshift centre-forward in Ueda's absence and could continue in that position if the latter fails to recover in time, although veteran striker Olivier Giroud also provides an alternative.

Meanwhile, Lyon will be without Tyler Morton, who recently underwent surgery for an abductor problem, while Pavel Sulc is recovering from a meniscus injury and Mohamed Ouedraogo is sidelined for the remainder of the campaign after rupturing his cruciate ligament.

Lois Openda also remains unavailable as he recovers from a fractured fibula, although the forward is expected to return in the coming weeks, while Steeve Kango could be available after rejoining group training following a period under concussion protocol.

Lille possible starting lineup:.

Ozer; Ngoy, Nianzou, Alexsandro, Perraud; Bentaleb, Andre, Mukau; E Mbappe, Haraldsson, Diaoune.

Greif; Athekame, Niakhate, Bacher, A Vinicius; Tessmann, Bidstrup, Tolisso; Nuamah, Merah, Nakamura.

Lyon's recent dominance in this fixture makes the visitors difficult to dismiss, particularly with Vicens hoping to make an immediate impression in his first match at the helm.

However, Lille's superior defensive record, unbeaten home form and greater consistency in the league should give Ancelotti's side the edge, and we expect the hosts to secure a narrow victory.

Michael Carrick has come under immense pressure as a disjointed Manchester United sit just two places above the relegation places.

Despite the scrutiny and the news of a possible sacking, Michael Carrick has been given another chance at Manchester United.

Michael Carrick will remain in charge of Manchester United for their Premier League trip to Chelsea on Saturday after the club decided to give their under-pressure head coach another opportunity to turn things around.

United have gone eight games without a win in all competitions, with Sunday’s humiliating 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth leaving them 16th in the Premier League table, just one point above the relegation zone.

Carrick’s position looked increasingly uncertain after the Bournemouth loss. As a result, United chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox were at Carrington on Monday to discuss the situation.

It has been reported by Sky Sports that United have considered other options internally as well to replace Micahel Carrick but for the weekend, they are sticking with Michael Carrick.

Carrick took training on Tuesday and the decision means he has at least one more match to convince the club’s hierarchy that he can get United back on track.

Gary Neville admitted he was surprised that Carrick had survived the immediate threat of losing his job, although he welcomed the decision.

“I am surprised, but I am happy because I was absolutely certain that what I witnessed on Sunday would be the end of Michael,” Neville stated in Sky Sports.

The former United captain explained that Carrick’s actions after the Bournemouth defeat had made him think the manager was preparing to say goodbye to the supporters.

“It looked like he was walking round at the end on his own with the players behind him, like it was almost a goodbye lap,” Neville added.

Fans continued singing the manager’s name after the final whistle, while the rest of the team drew boos.

Despite his surprise, Gary Neville hopes Micahel Carrick can use the extra time to get a response from his squad.

“I hope he can somehow get those players to start playing for him again because they haven’t played for him in the last few weeks,” he said.

The trip to Chelsea now becomes a crucial test for Micahel Carrick but United need a result and a far better performance to ease the pressure at Old Trafford.

Director of football Jason Wilcox and chief executive Omar Berrada discussed his position at the training ground the following day and agreed to give him three matches to turn things around before the break.

According to recent reports, those games brought a 2-0 defeat at Chelsea, a 3-2 win over Roma and a chaotic 4-4 draw with Aston Villa at Old Trafford on Sunday. United conceded eight goals across the three fixtures, and defensive frailty remains the biggest worry.

Industry observers note that the league table makes grim reading. United sit in the Premier League relegation zone with just one league win in their last 10 matches.

Sources indicate that if he does win a stay of execution, results will need to follow. Manchester United cannot be languishing in 17th place.

“I think there’s more than enough [to turn things around].”.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The Stags are at the moment in the midst of a third successive campaign in League One, with Nigel Clough's side amassing 19 points from 12 matches.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mansfield Town have made a decision to decrease the capacity of the One Call Stadium, otherwise known as Field Mill, after a meeting with the Safety Advisory Group.

The Stags are at the moment in the midst of a third successive campaign in League One, with Nigel Clough's side amassing 19 points from 12 matches.

As a result of the club's recent trajectory, Mansfield have welcomed several fallen giants to this part of Nottinghamshire.

Stags fans have developed a reputation for generating plenty of noise, which, in turn, has led to a strong atmosphere with those backing the visiting sides housed in the stadium's North Stand.

However, the decision, which has been made ahead of Saturday's clash with MK Dons, hasn't gone down well with several fans.

The One Call Stadium is currently the fifth-smallest stadium in League One, with only the home grounds of Cambridge United, Stevenage, Burton Albion and Bromley able to house fewer spectators.

Attendances so far this season have been at the 8,527 mark on average, but Mansfield will now see fewer visiting supporters pass through the turnstiles.

A statement from Nottinghamshire Council on Friday confirmed that the stadium's North Stand will be reduced in capacity from 1,000 to 600 following incidents relating to crowd management and control in the EFL Trophy clash against Chesterfield, which the League Two side won 5-3.

Mansfield have since confirmed the agreement in conjunction with the council and Safety Advisory Group, but also confirmed that the club are exploring the possibility of a safe-standing area within the stand.

Although this decision doesn't have a major impact on the matchday experience of the home support at the One Call Stadium, other than the fact there are fewer visiting fans to engage in back-and-forth with, it has caused plenty of responses.

One Stags supporter wrote: "SAG vs Mansfield Town yet again. Do they ever work with the club rather than against it?".

"But why? What was said in the meeting? Away fans getting punished by the SAG which reflects on the club? They deserve a bit of clarity," another commented.

"Poor decision and tbh, it’s rarely full," backed up the feeling of confusion as to why such measures have been taken.

Another Mansfield fan debated: "Surely (has) to be done up and down the country then?

Recent findings suggest that "There is literally nothing wrong with away fans standing up. SAG need to give their head a wobble," was one of many strong reactions.

Recent findings suggest that with Mansfield's last two home games coming against the Spireites and Notts County, another questioned: "Did SAG not look at who the last 3 games have been against at home? At least 2 they should’ve known it would’ve been an issue.".

Industry observers note that one of the potential fans visiting from Buckinghamshire on Saturday noted: "What('s) wrong with standing up? No need to close off part of the stand because of it.".

What do you make of Mansfield Town's decision to reduce the One Call Stadium's capacity? Comment below!

However, a Port Vale fan agreed with the decision, replying: "The ticket regulations say that fans should be sitting down. If they stand up and refuse to sit then have them thrown out. If they refuse to leave then have police arrest them. Don't punish other fans because there are some idiots.".

Although Mansfield clarified that the allocation will be temporarily reduced, it has already been debated for how long this will be the case.

Recent fixtures have clearly impacted this decision, and some of League One's largest fanbases could be left scrambling for tickets depending on how long such measures are in place.

Indeed, the Stags are still yet to host the likes of Barnsley, Sheffield Wednesday and Leicester City, with it not exactly being an arduous journey for those who follow the Tykes, Owls and Foxes to make.

Michael Carrick arrived at Carrington for Manchester United training as normal on Tuesday morning, while his bosses were preparing to decide his future in talks on the Mediterranean.

The club insists the Monaco summit was pre-planned and is not solely about the head coach and while that may be true, it hardly matters.By allowing the meeting to become public knowledge, United have turned a straightforward football decision into unnecessary drama, compounding an already difficult situation.

Carrick deserves better than this.Whatever the outcome, a club that wants to be taken seriously should not be settling its manager’s future in the full glare of the media while he is still out on the training pitch.

Depending on Alonso’s formation, Pedro Neto could operate either out on the right flank or in a central attacking role next to Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer, while Estevao Willian is another attacking option pushing to start.

Recent findings suggest that if Pedro is not fit to start, then Danny Welbeck will hope to earn a place up front after netting a brace in Chelsea’s 6-3 EFL Cup win over Leeds in September. However, Alonso may prefer to use both Rogers and Palmer in central positions – Palmer also scored twice in that cup tie against Leeds while Rogers provided four second-half assists.

Martinez; Acheampong, Fofana, Colwill; Neto, Caicedo, Henderson, Palestra; Estevao, Rogers, Palmer.

“The optics of being in Monaco whilst the team, the staff, the people who are running the club on a day-to-day basis are in Manchester, it’s just not good and it reflects badly on the leadership,” he remarked.

It’s more than an episode, it’s an omnishambles that reflects the dysfunctional state of MUFC in its current guise.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By MICHAEL PAVITT, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 09:50 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 06:26 EST, 16 November 2026.

Erling Haaland delivered a monologue of over two minutes detailing the teams he represented in the years covered by the Premier League's investigation into Man City, as the star questioned how he was meant to respond to the club's guilty verdict.

Man City were found guilty of the vast majority of charges brought against them by the Premier League for financial wrongdoing when the verdict was released in September. The club have since appealed.

An independent commission ruled Man City had disguised payments worth £900million in a nine-year period with ‘sham’ deals.

Man City were found to have artificially inflated sponsorship agreements and pumped money into the club from its Abu Dhabi owners via disguised payments in a bid to swerve Premier League spending rules.

Haaland was quizzed about the club's situation by Norwegian broadcaster TV2, after scoring in the national team's 3-1 victory over Wales on Saturday.

The Man City star's initial answer lasted for two minutes and 14 seconds, as he reeled off the teams he had represented from 2009 to 2018, the years covered by the charges.

In a recent development, erling Haaland insisted it was difficult for him to answer a question about Man City's guilty verdict, with the club appealing against the decision of an independent commission. Source: TV2Sport.

Haaland stressed he remains happy at the club after being asked about his future given the potential ramificiations if Man City fail with their appeal to overturn the verdict.

Sources indicate that 'In 2009, I played for Bryne U9s. In 2010, the U10s. In 2011, the U11s. 2012, the U12s, 2013, the U13s. Shall we continue? We don't need the whole list. 2014, the U14s. 2015, the U15s and the national team,' Haaland began.

'Then the U16s, I think. In 2016, I moved up to Bryne's first team, second team and youth team. In 2017, I went to Molde. In 2018, I was with Molde. The first team, Molde 2 and a bit with the youth team.

'So this is a question I struggle to answer because it's a legal battle….

According to recent reports, 'It's a case between the Premier League and Manchester City that a panel will deal with. Am I supposed to answer that? I'm not really sure.'.

Haaland continued by listing fellow Norwegians who had been at Man City at the time, joking that they may be in a better place to offer insight.

'There were quite a few Norwegians at the club during that period, I think,' Haaland said.

'Abdisalam Ibrahim, Martin Samuelsen and Omar Elabdellaoui were there. Kjetil Haug was there too. I think there were a couple more but I can't remember.

The forward distanced himself from the case as he listed team he played from 2009-18, the time covered by the charges. Pictured: Haaland in action for Molde in 2018.

'But it's a difficult question to answer when I don't really know that much about it.

'I assume the answers will come… I don't know when. I haven't read much about it.

'To be completely honest, I'm focused on trying to perform for Manchester City.

'A club I signed a five-year deal with in 2022 and a upcoming nine-and-a-half-year deal in late 2024. I think that states everything about the matter. I'm a City player, and I'm incredibly happy there.'.

Man City have continued to insist they had 'irrefutable evidence' proving their innocence, but if the club loses its appeal, the Premier League have a range of sanctions at their disposal – including relegation or expulsion.

Haaland, who has won eight major honours at the club including the Treble in 2023, was asked about whether the case has affected his thoughts on his Man City future.

'I understand that you want a little headline here, but as I mentioned, I signed a long-term contract in 2024,' Haaland responded.

Sources indicate that 'I'd say I made a pretty good choice by joining City in 2022. We can all agree on that. I won't say it myself, but look at the trophies I've won and how I've developed on and off the pitch.

'I'm standing here after winning an international 3-1 and we're top of our group in Europe.

According to recent reports, 'Things aren't going so well for City in the league, but we'll try to turn that around against Fulham. But we can't focus on that now. Now we have to focus on Denmark.'.

Man City have won twice and lost three times in the Premier League since the independent commission verdict was unveiled in September.

Enzo Maresca's side have slipped to six points behind reigning champions Arsenal following their drop off in form.

Industry observers note that the 54-year-old will replace Michael Carrick, who was dismissed on Thursday following United’s disastrous start to the Premier League season. Pochettino is set to sign a two-and-a-half-year contract that will keep him at Old Trafford until the summer of 2029.

It has been revealed that pochettino brings considerable Premier League experience after previous spells with Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea. He has also managed Paris Saint-Germain before the USA job.

His appointment makes him Manchester United’s eighth permanent manager since Sir Alex Ferguson retired in 2013.

Carrick’s departure came less than six months after he signed a two-year contract. His second spell in charge ended after United managed just one win in their opening 10 league matches, leaving them in the relegation zone.

Carrick’s coaching staff, including Jonny Evans, Jonathan Woodgate, Steve Holland, Travis Binnion and goalkeeping coach Craig Mawson, have all left alongside Carrick.

Barnsley have confirmed that adult tickets for their game against Huddersfield Town next month will cost £35.

The Tykes have had a tough season so far, with Daniel Stendel’s return to Oakwell not producing the results that many had hoped, as the team sit in the relegation zone.

However, many fans recognise that Barnsley’s problems run deeper right now, and there are calls for the owners to leave the club.

Whilst the criticism towards those at the top of the club is wide-ranging, one aspect that has left fans annoyed is the price it costs to watch games.

And, that has ignited again, with the club confirming that adult tickets for the home clash against Huddersfield on December 19 will be £35.

This was always going to be a game that was priced higher than most, as there is a rivalry between the two Yorkshire clubs - and it’s worth noting it’s the same pricing structure as the one they went with against Sheffield Wednesday.

Plus, with Huddersfield flying high, they are likely to shift a lot of tickets, so Barnsley, who will be charging the visitors £35 as well, will see this as a chance to make money.

Firstly, it should be said that problems with ticket prices are not exclusive to Barnsley, and fans of clubs up and down the country would want their own clubs to review prices.

But, in this instance, you can understand why Barnsley fans are furious, as £35 is an awful lot of money to watch a League One fixture.

Yes, it’s a game against a local side, but Barnsley are battling to stay in the third tier right now, so they should be doing all they can to bring supporters back, which isn’t going to happen when you’re charging £35.

Industry observers note that plus, this is a game that will be played a week before Christmas, at a time when money is tight for everyone. When you combine that with the fixture being televised, it really is a poor decision from Barnsley, who are prioritising money over fans.

Again, they’re by no means the only club to do that, but it’s a shame that they aren’t going the other way and trying to do affordable deals to entice supporters back.

Of course, the hierarchy will argue that they need to bring in funds to help the club, but it’s always about striking the right balance and making fans feel valued.

#2937. Liverpool vs Man United: Why England's biggest rivalry still matters amid United crisis

Liverpool vs Man United: Why England's biggest rivalry still matters amid United crisis

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1002 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Naim Beneddra | 19 Nov 2026 16:09.
  • Liverpool and Manchester United will renew one of English football's fiercest rivalries at Anfield on Sunday, but rarely have the two clubs approached this fixture from such contrasting positions.
  • Liverpool sit fourth in the Premier League under Andoni Iraola, while United arrive in the relegation zone following a disastrous start to the 2026-27 campaign that cost Michael Carrick his job.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Naim Beneddra | 19 Nov 2026 16:09.

Liverpool and Manchester United will renew one of English football's fiercest rivalries at Anfield on Sunday, but rarely have the two clubs approached this fixture from such contrasting positions.

Liverpool sit fourth in the Premier League under Andoni Iraola, while United arrive in the relegation zone following a disastrous start to the 2026-27 campaign that cost Michael Carrick his job.

Mauricio Pochettino's appointment has offered supporters renewed hope, although the Argentine could hardly have been handed a more demanding introduction. His first match in charge will be against the club United have historically regarded as their greatest rivals.

The circumstances are extraordinary. United have collected just eight points from their opening 10 league matches, winning only once, and are already 10 points behind Sunday's opponents.

Yet the gulf in the table has done little to diminish the significance of the occasion.

For Liverpool and United supporters, this fixture has never depended entirely on league positions. Its importance comes from generations of competition for domestic supremacy, the history of two neighbouring cities and the enduring desire to establish which club holds the greater place in English football.

Debates about England's greatest football rivalry inevitably produce different answers.

Arsenal and Tottenham Hotspur share one of the country's most intense local rivalries. Newcastle United and Sunderland have a derby rooted deeply in regional identity, while Manchester City and United have spent recent decades competing for the same major honours.

The historic tensions between Leeds United and Manchester United, or between Liverpool and Everton, are equally significant to the supporters involved.

Liverpool against United, however, occupies a distinctive position because it combines the prestige of two of England's most successful clubs with a rivalry between cities that predates professional football.

Liverpool developed into one of Britain's principal ports, while Manchester became an industrial powerhouse during the 19th century.

The opening of the Manchester Ship Canal in 1894 allowed goods to reach Manchester without passing through Liverpool's docks, becoming an enduring symbol of the economic competition between the two cities.

Football subsequently provided another arena for that rivalry.

Liverpool dominated English football during the 1970s and 1980s, winning league championships and European Cups while United struggled to match their domestic consistency.

The balance shifted dramatically under Sir Alex Ferguson.

United won 13 Premier League titles between 1993 and 2013, overtaking Liverpool's longstanding record of 18 English league championships in the process.

Ferguson's ambition to surpass Liverpool helped define United's most successful era, with the two clubs competing for supremacy even when they were not direct rivals for the title in a particular season.

Liverpool eventually ended their 30-year wait for a league championship under Jurgen Klopp in 2020 and drew level with United on 20 English top-flight titles by winning another in 2025.

That shared record has reinforced a rivalry measured across decades rather than individual seasons.

The head-to-head figures also demonstrate how closely contested the fixture has been historically.

Across 218 competitive meetings, United have recorded 85 victories to Liverpool's 72, with another 61 matches ending level.

However, those overall figures tell only part of the story.

Liverpool's extraordinary 7-0 victory at Anfield in March 2023 remains the largest winning margin in the fixture's history, while United demonstrated their ability to upset their rivals with a 3-2 victory at Old Trafford in May this year.

Results of that magnitude become part of the clubs' collective memories, ensuring that each newly introduced encounter carries the weight of previous triumphs and humiliations.

Sunday's meeting arrives at a particularly delicate moment for Manchester United.

The club's decision to replace Carrick with Pochettino reflects the scale of its problems, with a single Premier League victory leaving the Red Devils fighting to escape the bottom three.

The former Tottenham Hotspur and Chelsea manager officially began work on November 18, giving him only a few days to assess his squad before travelling to Merseyside.

As previously examined in Sports Mole's analysis of Pochettino's appointment and his preferred approach, the Argentine has built much of his reputation around pressing, collective organisation and developing young players.

Those principles will take time to establish, particularly in a squad that has struggled defensively throughout the campaign.

Anfield nevertheless provides an immediate opportunity to change the atmosphere surrounding the club.

A positive result would not erase United's difficult start, but taking points away from Liverpool could offer Pochettino an early foundation on which to build.

Defeat, particularly a heavy one, would bring another wave of scrutiny to a side already facing questions about its competitiveness.

Liverpool have their own reasons to attach considerable importance to the match.

Iraola, who replaced Klopp's successor Arne Slot in the summer, is preparing for his first competitive encounter with United as Liverpool manager.

His team remain in the Champions League positions, although their fourth-place standing leaves them with ambitions of closing the gap on the leaders.

Sunday therefore represents an important test of Liverpool's progress under their latest coach, as well as an opportunity to deepen their rivals' difficulties.

The stakes are different from those during the Ferguson era, when United regularly pursued championships, or the period when Liverpool were establishing themselves as Europe's dominant force.

But the nature of the rivalry means that United's current league position cannot make the match an ordinary fixture.

Both managers will experience this contest from their respective dugouts for the first time, while Pochettino faces the added challenge of beginning his United career in one of English football's most unforgiving away environments.

When Liverpool and Manchester United meet at Anfield on Sunday at 4.30pm, their immediate objectives will be markedly different.

Industry observers note that for Liverpool, victory would strengthen their position near the top of the Premier League. For United, the occasion offers a chance to begin repairing a damaged season.

The rivalry itself has survived far greater changes in the fortunes of both clubs, and Sunday's encounter will be another reminder of why their meetings continue to command such attention.

It has been revealed that never mind the lack of an ice vest, George Russell is somehow going to need to be the coolest man in Malaysia if he is to turn seventh on the grid into a positive result in Sunday’s Bahrain Grand Prix.The first race in Sepang in nearly a decade – a late addition to the calendar because of the conflict in the Middle East – promises to be an absolute scorcher. Russell might need something wacky if he is to do anything from that far back. This was a desperately disappointing result for the British driver. After his victory in Baku last weekend, Russell was hopeful he had finally found the winning formula and that he could continue to take the fight to his team-mate Kimi Antonelli, whom he trails in the drivers’ championship by 66pts.

It has been revealed that eighth, four places behind, and 0.24sec slower than the Italian, was not what Russell would have had in mind, although both Mercedes drivers will rise a spot because of the five-place grid penalty meted out to Red Bull’s Isack Hadjar for exceeding his engine allowance for the season.Russell will have felt particularly disappointed as Antonelli only got one run in Q3 after using up a set of soft tyres when he made a mistake and went off track in Q2. In a recent development, toto Wolff, the Mercedes team principal, admitted it was a head-scratcher. “Very difficult to understand,” the Austrian remarked. “We have been a little bit caught out on Friday with some car behaviour that we did not see all year, but then you can say it is very hot and the tarmac is different to all the [other] tracks. It looked really good this morning. We seemed to have, at least with Kimi, made a step in understanding. And then, qualifying was a little bit back to what we saw before, just no performance.”.

It has been revealed that still, both titles are in the bag so Wolff cannot be too unhappy. Russell is the one who will be really miffed. He really needs to be beating his team-mate pretty much every race weekend if he is to get his title hopes back on track.

According to recent reports, at the front, the mood was somewhat different. Verstappen became the first non-Mercedes-powered pilot to take a pole position this year. The last time a F1 held a race was held here back in 2017, the British driver claimed pole only to be overhauled by a youthful Verstappen. He will be desperate to turn the tables this time.

I will try my best to hold on to Max tomorrow, and if we are in the fight that would be awesome. I’ve been talking too much, but I guess you talk more when you are happy. It was my best lap of the year. It feels like I won, and I will give it everything tomorrow.”.

Recent findings suggest that it is Russell, though, who needs a result even more badly if he is to remain a factor in the championship. “As a team, we have yet to have a bad race this whole season and this was clearly a very bad qualifying for us,” he admitted, adding that “all the numbers” from the upgrade package suggested it was an improvement on the old car. “But I think there is going to be a lot happening tomorrow.
